title: Crystalloid vs colloid for Hemodynamics during Anesthesia INduction in TAVR patients (CHAIN-T): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
authors: Xiaoshuang Tuo; Fahan Wang; Youjun Chen; Min Chen; Zhihong Lu
abstract:
To assess whether preload with colloids could reduce hypotension during induction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) compared to crystalloids.
This study is a single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel-controlled trial conducted at Xijing Hospital. A total of 116 patients scheduled for elective TAVR under general anesthesia will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the colloid group or the crystalloid group, receiving either 5 ml/kg of colloid or crystalloid solution before anesthesia induction infused over 15 min. The primary outcome is the area under curve (AUC) of the change in mean arterial pressure (MAP) from baseline during the induction period (until 15 min after induction). Secondary outcomes include the incidence of intraoperative hemodynamic instability, the use of intraoperative vasoactive drugs, the Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on the first postoperative day, postoperative hospital length of stay, the rate of intensive care unit (ICU) admission postoperatively, all-cause mortality during hospitalization and by 30 days after surgery, and the incidence of renal replacement therapy by 30 days after surgery.
The results of this study will provide evidence on optimizing fluid preload to prevent hypotension during induction, reduce postoperative complications, and enhance recovery for patients undergoing TAVR. The findings are expected to promote anesthesia protocols in this patient population.
The study protocol and statistical analysis plan were approved by the institutional Ethics Committee of Xijing Hospital, Fourth Military Medical University (XJLL-KY-20252560). The study was registered in ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT07329660) on December 29, 2025.

title: Neurological manifestations and vasculopathy in PLCG2-associated antibody deficiency and immune dysregulation (APLAID): a case series.
authors: Kosar Asna Ashari; Rebecca MacRae; David P Hoytema van Konijnenburg; Craig D Platt; Maryam Ashoor; Alfred P See; Agnieszka Kielian; Amy Danehy; Riten Kumar; Elliot James; Kristin Houghton; Sheri Harder; Mark P Gorman; Stacy A Kahn; Ankana Daga; Sadaf H Hussain; Alicia M Johnston; Alicia Casey; Jodie D Ouahed; Wai Wong; Kathy Jenkins; Susan Prockop; Esraa Eloseily; Kimberly Risma; Michael J Ombrello; Fatma Dedeoglu; Milena M Andzelm
abstract:
Autosomal dominant pathogenic variants in PLCG2 are associated with autoinflammation and PLCG2-associated antibody deficiency and immune dysregulation (APLAID), characterized by immunological abnormalities and multi-system inflammation. Descriptions of associated neurological manifestations and vascular anomalies are limited. We describe three patients with APLAID, vasculopathies, neuroinflammation, and cerebral vascular tortuosity. These cases highlight underrecognized and clinically important manifestations of APLAID.
All three patients had de novo variants in PLCG2 and early systemic inflammatory and immunodeficiency findings within the spectrum of APLAID (e.g. immune laboratory abnormalities, skin and gastrointestinal inflammation, and frequent infections). Additionally, they had notable neurological and vascular findings. Patient #1 (PLCG2 c.3420T > A; p.Asp1140Glu) is a female who had focal seizures at 16 months old. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) revealed right parietal leptomeningeal enhancement with white matter changes. MR angiography (MRA) showed cerebrovascular tortuosity and stenoses without evidence of vasculitis. She had extensive veno-lymphatic malformation in the thorax, abnormal renal vasculature, inferior vena cava (IVC) atresia, and bilateral pulmonary vein stenosis (PVS). Patient #2 (PLCG2 c.2122G > C; p.Ala708Pro) is a male who at four years old had an episode of status epilepticus. MRI revealed a right parietal infarct with surrounding leptomeningeal enhancement and MRA demonstrated abnormal caliber of the right middle cerebral artery (MCA), arterial tortuosity, and carotid aneurysms. His course was complicated by aortic root dilation and bilateral PVS. Patient #3 (PLCG2 c.2122G > C; p.Ala708Pro) is a male who at 16 months had a right sided focal motor seizure. MRI demonstrated infarct with associated sulcal enhancement predominantly in the left cerebral hemisphere. MRA found excessive vascular tortuosity and fenestrations. He has a dilated aortic root and ventricular septal defect (VSD).
We present three cases of APLAID complicated by significant cerebrovascular tortuosity and seizure and two with cerebral ischemia. The etiology of stroke and/or seizures in these patients is unclear, but vasculopathy leading to perfusion deficits, neuroinflammation, or thrombosis due to underlying thrombotic diathesis or abnormal vascular anatomy may have contributed. We recommend all patients with APLAID undergo monitoring for neurologic manifestations. Additionally, we highlight important vasculopathic findings such as PVS, where early recognition for directed treatment is critical.

title: Refractory rapidly progressive diffuse in-stent restenosis with left main involvement: a case report.
authors: Xiaoyan Wang; Haichao Yang; Liqiang Qin; Wei Lu; Lijun Wang; Jianjun Wang; Juan Li; Kaibin Deng; Chenguang Gao
abstract:
Drug-eluting stents (DES) have significantly reduced the incidence of in-stent restenosis (ISR). However, a subset of patients still develop refractory, rapidly progressive, and diffuse ISR, which poses substantial therapeutic challenges and reflects its complex underlying mechanisms.
We report a 46-year-old male who underwent five percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) over five years, with repeated diffuse ISR in the left anterior descending artery (LAD). Initial PCI was followed by DCB therapy after first ISR, achieving temporary symptom relief. Four years later, ISR progressed to chronic total occlusion, requiring further stenting and DCB therapy. Within five months, he developed 99% LM stenosis and recurrent LAD ISR. Despite a SYNTAX score of 36 favoring CABG, the patient refused surgery. Under intra-aortic balloon pump support, a balloon-only PCI (stent-less) strategy was performed. IVUS revealed diffuse fibrous proliferation and neoatherosclerosis. During follow-up, the patient remained clinically stable overall.
This case highlights a potential systemic hyperproliferative phenotype, in which repeated vascular injury triggers accelerated neoatherosclerosis and intimal hyperplasia. It challenges the conventional view of ISR as a local mechanical problem and underscores the importance of mechanism-driven risk stratification and individualized management, particularly when standard surgical therapy is declined.

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Valvular Heart Disease: Assessing the Impact of Genetics in the UK Biobank.
authors: Luca Cristin; Janet J Tang; Lionel Tastet; Rohit Jhawar; David V Glidden; Gregory M Marcus; Francesca N Delling
abstract:
Atrial fibrillation (AF) in valvular heart disease (VHD) is generally attributed to pressure or volume overload with atrial remodeling, but the independent contribution of genetic predisposition remains unclear.
The authors evaluated the predictive value of a previously developed AF polygenic risk score (PRS) across VHD subtypes in the UK Biobank.
In this prospective cohort study (UK Biobank, 2000-2022), incident AF and VHD status were defined using ICD codes. VHD subtypes included mitral valve (MV) disease (MV prolapse [MVP], mitral regurgitation, mitral stenosis) and aortic valve (AV) disease (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation). PRS was categorized into quintiles and grouped as low, intermediate, and high.
Among 452,841 participants with available PRS, 385 had MVP, 1,058 mitral regurgitation, 81 mitral stenosis, 421 aortic regurgitation, and 509 aortic stenosis. In Cox models, PRS was independently associated with incident AF in MV disease (HR: 1.7, P = 0.03 for intermediate PRS; HR: 2.3, P = 0.002 for high PRS), with the strongest effect in MVP (HR: 3.1, P = 0.03 for high PRS). In AV disease, PRS was not significantly associated with AF risk (P = 0.93 and P = 0.07 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively). Interaction analyses confirmed attenuation or absence of the PRS effect in AV disease (P = 0.04 and P = 0.004 for intermediate and high PRS, respectively), whereas no significant interaction was observed in MV disease (P = 0.80 and P = 0.11, respectively).
In VHD, AF PRS predicts AF risk, but the genetic impact differs by subtype. AV disease shows minimal genetic contribution, suggesting predominantly hemodynamic risk, while MV disease-particularly MVP-shows substantial genetic influence.

title: Impact of Coronary Artery Disease on Long-Term Valve Function After the Ozaki Procedure: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study (2015 - 2020).
authors: Vladlen Bazylev; Artur Mikulyak; Khadiev M Dzhokhar; Yazan Khanfar; Vadim Karnakhin
abstract:
The Ozaki procedure reconstructs the aortic valve with autologous pericardium, but long-term leaflet durability remains uncertain. Coronary artery disease (CAD) may reflect a systemic atheroinflammatory milieu associated with impaired leaflet integrity.
We retrospectively studied 733 patients undergoing Ozaki reconstruction from 2015 to 2020 and assessed the association between CAD and aortic regurgitation (AR) ≥ 2 at last echocardiographic follow-up. Baseline heterogeneity was addressed using propensity-score overlap weighting based on age, sex, body mass index, body surface area, weight, diabetes, European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II, aortic stenosis, bicuspid valve, and peripheral artery disease. Effects were estimated as weighted risk ratios (RRs) using Poisson models with robust variance. Sensitivity analyses used stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and an extended model including prior myocardial infarction/percutaneous coronary intervention.
Of 733 patients, 365 (49.8%) had CAD. Unadjusted AR > 2 rates were 10.1% in CAD vs. 5.7% in no-CAD patients (P = 0.037). After overlap weighting, weighted risks were 12.7% vs. 6.2%, yielding RR 2.05 (95% CI, 1.01 - 4.18; P = 0.048), with excellent covariate balance. IPTW showed consistent results: RR 2.22 (95% CI, 1.38 - 3.56; P = 0.001). Regurgitation-free survival was lower in CAD patients (log-rank P = 0.0087).
CAD was associated with an approximately two-fold higher risk of AR ≥ 2 after Ozaki reconstruction. This association likely reflects systemic atheroinflammatory processes rather than a direct mechanical effect, supporting closer postoperative surveillance in CAD patients.

title: Diagnostic performance of aortic valve calcium and CT-derived aortic valve area in low-gradient aortic stenosis.
authors: Dakota De Cecco; Christopher Scoma; Corey Powell; Megan Joseph; William Truesdell; Stanley Chetcuti; Andrew W Harris
abstract:
Practice guidelines recommend the use of computed tomography (CT) aortic valve calcium (AVC) scores for patients with low-gradient aortic stenosis (LG-AS). AVC has not been studied in comparison to invasive aortic valve study (IAVS).
To determine the diagnostic performance of AVC and CT-derived aortic valve area (CT-AVA) compared to IAVS as a reference standard.
We included consecutive patients with LG-AS with echocardiography, CT and IAVS performed within 1 year at a single tertiary center. Severe AS was defined by aortic valve area (AVA) ≤1.0 cm2 measured by IAVS. CT-AVA was retrospectively measured by a blinded reader. CT-AVA and sex-based AVC were compared to AS defined by IAVS. Diagnostic performance was compared using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. AVC and CT-AVA were compared to cardiac events consisting of death, aortic valve replacement and cardiovascular hospitalization.
Out of 294 patients in the overall cohort, 206 patients with definite AS severity by IAVS were included as the primary diagnostic cohort. Severe AS according to invasive AVA (≤1.0 cm2) was present in 72 patients (35.0%). Sex-based AVC scores had relatively poor diagnostic performance compared to the reference IAVS with AUCs of 0.59 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.48-0.70) and 0.58 (95% CI 0.45-0.71) for men and women, respectively. CT-AVA had better diagnostic performance with an AUC of 0.82 (95% CI 0.77-0.87).
In our study population, CT-AVA had significantly better diagnostic performance than AVC compared to the reference standard, IAVS.

title: In-Hospital Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement Surgical Versus Transcatheter: A Nationwide Study with Machine Learning-Based Risk Prediction.
authors: Akash Sharma; Mohamed Jamshid Ubaid; Fnu Shalini; Hamza Yousaf
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) are two preferred methods for treating aortic stenosis. This study compared the in-hospital mortality rates associated with SAVR and TAVR.
In accordance with the STROBE guidelines, we conducted an analytical cross-sectional study utilizing data from the National Readmission Database (NRD) spanning from 2016 to 2020. Patients who underwent TAVR or SAVR were identified using specific ICD-10 procedure codes. We employed adjusted multivariate logistic regression analysis to determine the odds ratio (OR) of death associated with SAVR compared to TAVR. Patients were followed for a year and OR with 95% CI were calculated. AI based XGBoost model were used to find the predictors of mortality.
Our study included a total of 361,875 patients. Among these, 182,443 underwent TAVR, while 179,432 underwent SAVR. In the TAVR group, 2,563 patients (1.4%) died during hospitalization, whereas 6,671 patients (3.7%) died in the SAVR group. The multivariate logistic regression analysis indicated that SAVR is associated with higher in-hospital mortality (OR = 2.66, 95% CI 2.51-2.81, p < 0.001) compared to TAVR. Follow up data at 30 days, three months, six months, did not find any difference in mortality between TAVR and SAVR. Notably, liver failure, HLD, renal failure, SAVR, female, CHF, and atrial fibrillation are amongst the top predictor of mortality in patients undergoing (TAVR or SAVR). While in cardiac rehospitalization, risk factors like female gender, CHF, Afib, HLD, DM have higher predictability than procedure.
Our study demonstrates that SAVR is associated with a higher likelihood of in-hospital mortality compared to TAVR, with organ dysfunction (liver failure, kidney dysfunction) as a predictor of mortality.

title: Left Ventricular Assist Device Implantation in Dextrocardia: Lessons From a Complex Redo Case.
authors: Jun Fu; Zhixiang Gu; Jinpeng Li; Dongsi Shuang; Bao Sun; Yiliyasi Yimingjiang; Lin Chen
journal: ASAIO journal (American Society for Artificial Internal Organs : 1992)
abstract: Dextrocardia with situs solitus poses significant surgical challenges for left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation, particularly in patients with prior sternotomy and complex valvular disease. We report on a 60 year old man with dextrocardia, advanced heart failure, prior mechanical mitral valve replacement, and bicuspid aortic valve disease who underwent successful Corheart 6 LVAD implantation during redo sternotomy with concomitant bioprosthetic aortic and mitral valve replacement. Intraoperative findings included extensive pannus/thrombus on the mechanical mitral prosthesis (causing relative stenosis) and an unsuspected 10 g left atrial thrombus, both of which were removed. Total cardiopulmonary bypass time was 330 minutes, and aortic cross‑clamp time was 233 minutes. Postoperative acute kidney injury requiring dialysis resolved, and the patient was discharged after 137 days. At 1 year follow-up, the left ventricular end-diastolic diameter decreased from 69 to 66 mm, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) remained stable (28-25%), New York Heart Association (NYHA) class improved from IIIb‑IV to II, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) recovered from 32 ml/min at 9 months to 51 ml/min at 1 year.

title: Integrating volumes into myocardial work: the prognostic role of non-invasive pressure-strain-volume analysis in transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Tímea K Turschl; Zsuzsanna Ladányi; Andrea Ferencz; Alexandra Fábián; Márton Tokodi; Ádám Szijártó; Mihály Ruppert; Andrea Nagy; Andrea Á Molnár; Levente Molnár; Endre Zima; Attila Kovács; Bálint K Lakatos; Béla Merkely
abstract: The accurate echocardiographic assessment of the left ventricular (LV) contractile state remains challenging in aortic stenosis, as ejection fraction and even global longitudinal strain are markedly load-dependent. The novel pressure-strain loop-derived myocardial work were developed to overcome this limitation; however, incorporation of instantaneous LV volume may further improve this method. We aimed to quantify myocardial work using pressure-strain-volume (PSV) loops and to evaluate its prognostic value in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). We enrolled 300 patients scheduled for TAVI (age 78.7 ± 6.3 years, 41% female). The endpoint was all-cause mortality, reached by 62 patients over a median follow-up of 25 months. Echocardiography and non-invasive blood pressure measurements were performed one day before TAVI. LV pressure was estimated noninvasively, while strain curves were derived from speckle-tracking analysis. Pressure-strain relations were adjusted to instantaneous LV volumes to construct PSV loops, yielding volume-adjusted indices (GWIVi and GCWVi). GWIVi showed similar extent of LV dysfunction in classical and paradoxical low-flow low-gradient AS phenotypes compared to the normal flow-high gradient patients (46.98 ± 20.71 vs. 51.99 ± 18.43 vs. 63.74 ± 22.26 mmHg%L/m2, p < 0.001), while other LV function parameters did not. In multivariable Cox-regression, GWIVi was an independent predictor of mortality (Hazard ratio: 0.955 [confidence interval: 0.773-0.993], p < 0.05) alongside clinically relevant other markers such as hemoglobin and atrial fibrillation. PSV loop-derived myocardial work detected LV mechanical differences between AS phenotypes and provided independent prognostic value in TAVI candidates, potentially offering a more physiologically accurate assessment of LV function in this population.

title: Carotid atherosclerosis and aortic stiffness in masters athletes: Multimodality vascular phenotyping from the Master@Heart study.
authors: Rik Pauwels; Christophe Dausin; Ruben De Bosscher; Jarne De Paepe; Youri Bekhuis; Boris Delpire; Kasper Favere; Jürgen Duchenne; Thijs M H Eijsvogels; Peter Sinnaeve; Steven Dymarkowski; Olivier Ghekiere; Tatiana Kuznetsova; Caroline M Van De Heyning; Paul L Van Herck; Tomas Robyns; Lieven Herbots; André La Gerche; Hein Heidbuchel; Rik Willems; Guido Claessen
abstract:
Middle-aged male Masters athletes exhibit a higher burden of coronary atherosclerosis on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) compared with healthy controls. Whether this is accompanied by differences in carotid atherosclerosis or aortic stiffness remains uncertain. We assessed carotid atherosclerosis and aortic stiffness across groups, association between carotid atherosclerosis and coronary disease, and the incremental value of carotid plaque beyond traditional risk factors.
In this cross-sectional analysis of the Master@Heart study, 549 low cardiovascular risk men (median age 55 [50-60] years), including lifelong athletes, late-onset athletes, and healthy controls, underwent vascular phenotyping. Carotid plaque was assessed by ultrasound, aortic stiffness by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV), and coronary atherosclerosis by CCTA. Group differences were assessed using chi-square and Kruskal-Wallis tests. Association between carotid and coronary atherosclerosis was evaluated using regression models. Incremental discriminatory value was assessed using ROC curve analysis.
Prevalence of ≥1 carotid plaque did not differ between lifelong athletes, late-onset athletes, and controls (29.5%vs. 33.2% vs. 27.9%; p = 0.54). Carotid stenosis ≥50% was rare (1.2%-2.7%) and similar across groups (p = 0.54). Median PWV did not differ between groups (p = 0.29). Carotid plaque was associated with coronary atherosclerosis on CCTA. However, adding carotid plaque to traditional risk factors did not improve discrimination of coronary atherosclerosis.
In middle-aged male Masters athletes, excess subclinical coronary atherosclerosis is observed without corresponding differences in carotid plaque or aortic stiffness. Although carotid plaque is associated with coronary atherosclerosis, it does not meaningfully improve risk discrimination beyond traditional risk factors.

title: Arterial tortuosity syndrome with coronary artery involvement in a middle-aged female: A case report.
authors: Prinsa Shrestha; Amin Shah; Saroj Gc; Niraj Kumar Sharma; Aditya Mahaseth; Sanjaya Kumar Shrestha
abstract: Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective-tissue arteriopathy characterized by diffuse elongation and tortuosity of large and medium-sized arteries. Although it is typically diagnosed during childhood, adult presentation may occur and can be overlooked when overt connective-tissue manifestations are absent; coronary involvement is uncommon but clinically important. A 41-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of exertional substernal chest pain and dyspnea. CT coronary angiography demonstrated marked tortuosity of the left main coronary artery with focal kinking approximately 6.8 mm from its origin and 40-45% luminal stenosis (CAD-RADS 2). Contrast-enhanced CT angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrated generalized arterial elongation and marked tortuosity involving the thoracic aorta, supra-aortic branches, and abdominal aortic branches, together with early branching of the main pulmonary artery, without aneurysm, dissection, or intramural hematoma. Conventional coronary angiography was technically unsuccessful because of severe arterial tortuosity, with unsuccessful catheter advancement and coronary engagement despite radial and subsequent femoral access. The overall clinical and imaging findings were highly suggestive of ATS with coronary involvement, although molecular genetic confirmation was not available. The patient was managed conservatively with vascular risk-factor optimization and structured follow-up, with symptomatic improvement at one month. This case highlights that ATS may present in adulthood with coronary artery tortuosity and focal kinking and emphasizes the importance of recognizing diffuse multi-territory arterial tortuosity on CT. Comprehensive vascular imaging can establish a strong radiological suspicion of ATS, identify coronary involvement and procedural challenges, and guide surveillance even when genetic confirmation is unavailable.

title: Rapid Progression of Cardiac Allograft Vasculopathy With Sudden Cardiac Death Within the First Year of Heart Transplantation: A Case Report.
authors: Malcom Dix; Jean-Pierre Iskandar; Lefan He; Mohaned S Serdah; Aditya A Joshi; Anuradha Godishala; Abhishek Chaturvedi; Katherine Kaproth-Joslin; David A Dombroski; YeeAnn Chen; Wendy A Cheruiyot; Ronald Chong-Yik; Ronald G Schwartz; Jeffrey Alexis; Igor Gosev; Katherine L Wood; Sabu Thomas
abstract: Cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) is a major cause of mortality and morbidity within the first 3 years of heart transplantation (HT). CAV results in progressive coronary artery stenosis and may lead to arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. In some cases, sudden cardiac death represents the initial presentation of CAV, as cardiac denervation blunts anginal symptoms that otherwise could have preceded sudden cardiac death (SCD). Here, we describe the case of a 56-year-old man with non-ischemic cardiomyopathy. He underwent left ventricular assist device implantation followed by orthotopic HT. Five months after transplantation, he presented with atypical mid-sternal chest discomfort initially thought to be musculoskeletal in origin. Routine coronary angiography at 12 months revealed severe, diffuse 3-vessel disease consistent with International Society of Heart and Lung Transplantation (ISHLT) CAV-3, and cardiac MRI revealed full thickness delayed enhancement in the inferior wall consistent with infarction. Despite overall preserved left ventricular ejection fraction, he developed polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (VT) with an appropriate shock from a wearable cardioverter-defibrillator (WCD) and was transferred with an intra-aortic balloon pump to a larger transplant center and underwent another heart transplantation. This case highlights rapid CAV progression leading to infarction and arrhythmia despite preserved LVEF, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening with biomarkers and imaging as well as earlier consideration for device-based strategies to prevent sudden cardiac death in high-risk transplant recipients.

title: Achieving Reliable Peripheral Nerve Blockade in Cardiogenic Shock With Distorted Femoral Anatomy: A Case Report.
authors: Mohammed I Hakami; Ayman H Mustafa
abstract: Patients with cardiogenic shock and severe structural heart disease may poorly tolerate both general and neuraxial anesthesia. In selected cases, peripheral nerve blockade may reduce hemodynamic disturbance, but the block must be reliable when pain, sympathetic stimulation, or emergency conversion to general anesthesia could be poorly tolerated. We report a 62-year-old woman with cardiogenic shock, low-flow, low-gradient severe aortic stenosis, advanced dilated cardiomyopathy, pulmonary edema, orthopnea, and active femoral bleeding who required urgent femoral artery and vein repair. General anesthesia and neuraxial anesthesia were considered hazardous. Hematoma and anasarca distorted the femoral anatomy and prevented direct femoral nerve visualization. Combined ultrasound guidance and nerve stimulation were used to support safe needle advancement and functional nerve localization. Surgery proceeded with minimal sedation and without escalation of vasoactive support. This case highlights the role of reliability-focused peripheral nerve blockade when conventional anesthetic options are high risk and regional anatomy is distorted.

title: Construction and implantation of a modified trileaflet polytetrafluoroethylene valved conduit for pulmonary valve replacement.
authors: Abel Getachew; Nikita Zadneulitca; Ashok Muralidaran; Castigliano M Bhamidipati; Yoshio Ootaki
abstract:
Handmade expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) valved conduits have emerged as a durable and cost-effective option for pulmonary valve replacement. We have reported excellent results of trileaflet ePTFE valved conduit and the longest follow-up exceeded 10 years. Technical precision during valve construction and implantation is critical to optimize valve function and conduit geometry, and we recently modified the technique. We report our updated technique and clinical outcomes.
The conduit was constructed intraoperatively on a sterile back table while the patient was being prepared by the anesthesia team. Leaflet dimensions were calculated based on conduit diameter, and leaflets were fashioned with 1 mm extensions at each end to reinforce commissural attachment, then sutured to an ePTFE tube graft using 3 CV-5 sutures with external knot tying. The graft was rotated during construction to ensure accurate leaflet alignment and valve competence was confirmed prior to implantation. During implantation, the main pulmonary artery was divided to optimize conduit geometry, minimizing the posterior conduit length and the graft trimmed in a trapezoidal fashion to reduce tension and improve alignment.
Fifty-four patients received ePTFE valved conduit. Conduit sizes were 18 mm (n = 7), 20 mm (n = 9), 22 mm (n = 1), 24 mm (n = 36), and 28 mm (n = 1). Median follow-up was 1.4 years (maximum, 4.3 years). There was 1 mortality during follow-up due to infectious pseudoaneurysm of the aortic root after Ross procedure. One patient developed severe pulmonary insufficiency after surgery. Recent echocardiography showed no significant pulmonary stenosis, pulmonary insufficiency, or valve deterioration in the remaining patients, and no catheter-based or surgical reinterventions have been required to date.
This refined technique for the construction and implantation of a trileaflet ePTFE valved conduit is simple, reproducible, and yields excellent early hemodynamic results. Attention to leaflet design, commissural security, and conduit geometry may contribute to low early failure rates and favorable valve performance. Longer-term follow-up is ongoing to assess durability.

title: Prenatal diagnosis of mitral-pulmonary intervalvular fibrosa pseudoaneurysm associated with TGA causing severe pulmonary stenosis: A rare case report.
authors: Aliya Kemal Ahsan; Putri Yubbu; Anizah Aishah Rosli
abstract:
Pseudoaneurysm of the mitral-aortic intervalvular fibrosa is a rare and typically acquired cardiac lesion, with congenital forms being exceptionally uncommon, particularly when identified prenatally. We report the case of a 23-year-old gravida 2 woman with one previous history of miscarriage who was referred at 25 weeks' gestation for a fetal intracardiac mass. Fetal echocardiography revealed a cystic echogenic mass at the crux of the heart, consistent with a pseudoaneurysm arising from the mitral-pulmonary intervalvular fibrosa (MPIVF) associated with transposition of the great arteries, causing severe left ventricular outflow tract obstruction or subvalvular pulmonary stenosis. The cardiac lesion was also associated with a large mid-muscular ventricular septal defect alongside a small left ventricle suggestive of single-ventricle physiology. This constellation of findings pointed to a diagnosis of complex cyanotic congenital heart disease with possible ductal-dependent pulmonary circulation. Prenatal diagnosis enabled early parental counseling, planning for delivery at a tertiary cardiac center, and postnatal preparation for prostaglandin therapy and surgical evaluation. This case highlights the importance of recognizing MPIVF pseudoaneurysm in the fetal period, particularly when associated with obstructive physiology or major structural anomalies, and contributes to the limited literature on congenital variants of this condition.
Pseudoaneurysm of the mitral-pulmonary intervalvular fibrosa is an exceptionally rare congenital lesion. Its association with transposition of the great arteries, ventricular septal defect, and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction has important prognostic and surgical implications. Prenatal echocardiography is key for recognition, particularly when there is a cystic or echogenic intracardiac mass with a to-and-fro Doppler flow near the atrioventricular junction. Prenatal echocardiography is crucial for early counseling and planned delivery at a tertiary cardiac center.

title: Low-dose juglone attenuates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy through Lys207-dependent FoxO1 activation and mitochondrial protection.
authors: Hongyu Chen; Zhihao Yang; Cheng Zhang; Chengxin Ge; Yingliang Zhao; Shaopeng Cheng; Yilin Wang; Hao Chen; Can Xu; Dongjin Wang; Jie Yang
abstract: Pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and redox imbalance. Here, we investigated the efficacy, safety window, and redox-regulatory mechanism of juglone, a naturally occurring 5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone. In mice subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC), high-dose juglone induced cardiac, hepatic, and renal toxicity, whereas 1 mg/kg/day was well tolerated and attenuated cardiac hypertrophy. Juglone also suppressed Ang II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy in vitro and preserved mitochondrial ultrastructure and mitochondrial membrane potential, respiration, ATP production, and redox homeostasis. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) revealed that juglone reduced stress-associated cardiomyocyte states and enriched calcium-handling cardiomyocytes. Integrated transcriptomic analyses, Biotin-Juglone pull-down assay, surface plasmon resonance, cellular thermal shift assays, molecular docking, and mutational analyses identified FoxO1 as a functional target of juglone. Juglone engaged the FoxO1 DNA-binding domain in a Lys207-dependent manner, and was associated with FoxO1 deacetylation, nuclear accumulation, and transcriptional activation. Activated FoxO1 induced Sesn3 transcription and restored AMPK phosphorylation at Thr172. Sesn3 silencing markedly attenuated juglone-induced AMPK activation and impaired its protective effects against cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and mitochondrial dysfunction. FoxO1 silencing, FoxO1-K207Q mutation, blockade of FoxO1 deacetylation, or inhibition of FoxO1 transcriptional activity impaired these benefits. Importantly, myocardium from patients with aortic valve stenosis-associated hypertrophy exhibited increased FoxO1 acetylation, reduced cardiomyocyte nuclear FoxO1 localization, decreased Sesn3 expression and AMPK phosphorylation, and increased 4-HNE. Collectively, low-dose juglone attenuates pathological hypertrophy and preserves mitochondrial homeostasis through the FoxO1-Sesn3-AMPK axis, while highlighting the importance of dose-dependent redox effects in determining its therapeutic efficacy and systemic toxicity.

title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

authors: IGISINOV S.ZH.; RYSKELDIKYZY R.; GAISAGALEYEVA B.M.; UVALIYEVA G.M.; ZHUMABAYEVA ZH.O.
journal: Научный журнал "Вестник Актюбинского регионального университета имени К. Жубанова"
abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Prevalence of frailty syndrome among patients with severe aortic stenosis qualified for TAVI
authors: Natalia Świątoniowska-Lonc; Kinga Węgrzynowska‐Teodorczyk; Francesco Perone; Krzysztof Ściborski; Waldemar Banasiak; Adrian Doroszko
abstract: Abstract Background Frailty syndrome is a common comorbidity in elderly patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), significantly influencing outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Early identification of frailty and its determinants is essential for optimizing care and improving quality of life. Methods This cross-sectional, observational study included 113 Polish patients qualified for TAVI between January and September 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI). Quality of life, mental health, and social support were evaluated with TASQ, HADS, and MSPSS questionnaires. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of frailty. Results Frailty syndrome was present in 82.3% of patients. Higher frailty levels were associated with worse NYHA class, unhealthy lifestyle, and increased emotional burden. Depression and anxiety were significantly correlated with frailty, especially its psychological domain. Logistic regression revealed that NYHA class, emotional impact (TASQ), and unhealthy lifestyle were independent predictors of frailty. Social support negatively correlated with social frailty scores, suggesting a protective effect. Conclusions Frailty is highly prevalent among patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI. Comprehensive preprocedural assessment should include physical, emotional, and social factors. Targeted interventions - particularly prehabilitation and psychosocial support - may help address modifiable components of frailty in this population. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Preoperative Ballon Aortic Valvuloplasty vs. Conservative Management in Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery with Underlying Severe Aortic Stenosis
authors: Antonio De Vita; Marcello Covino; Francesco Mollo; Matteo Vumbaca; Chiara Napolitano; Saverio Tremamunno; Nello Cambise; Rosaria Natali; Marco Rossi; Tiziana Bove; Raffaele Vitiello; Giulio Maccauro; Francesco Franceschi; Carlo Trani; Francesco Burzotta; Gaetano Antonio Lanza
abstract: Background: Old adults with hip fracture (HFx) and concomitant severe aortic stenosis (AS) represent a high-risk population in whom urgent orthopedic repair is usually required, while definitive valve replacement is rarely feasible preoperatively. The clinical benefit of balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV) as a bridging strategy remains uncertain. Methods: In this observational study, we included patients admitted to our Emergency Department for HFx who had concomitant severe AS. Management of severe AS consisted of either conservative therapy or preoperative BAV. The early clinical endpoints included 30-day mortality, time to surgery, length of intensive care unit and hospital stay and need for mechanical ventilation. The late clinical endpoint was 180-day all-cause mortality. Results: Among 3958 patients admitted for HFx fracture, 46 (1.2%) were found to have severe AS and fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 patients (26.1%) underwent preoperative BAV and 34 (73.9%) received conservative management. Thirty-day mortality was 8.3% in the BAV group and 23.5% in the conservative group (HR 0.32; 95%CI 0.04–2.60; p = 0.29). Time to surgery was longer in the BAV group (p < 0.001) with concomitantly longer hospital (p = 0.001) and ICU (p = 0.041) stays. Preoperative BAV was independently associated with lower 180-day mortality (HR 0.13; 95%CI 0.03–0.63; p = 0.011). Conclusions: In patients with severe AS undergoing urgent HFx repair, preoperative BAV was associated with reduced 180-day mortality, suggesting a potential long-term prognostic benefit, which warrants confirmation in larger prospective studies. However, it was not associated with significantly better 30-day survival and was accompanied by surgical delay and greater healthcare resource utilization.

title: Case Report: Refractory childhood-onset takayasu arteritis with digital clubbing and extensive supra-aortic and lower-limb arterial disease
authors: Fawzy Mazen Abunejma; Leen M. Jabari; Marah Nouredeen Hamad; Tamer O. Tamimi; Omair Bseiso; Hisham Aziz Dweik; Raed M. A. Isayed; Hanan Qunibi; Waleed Alzaro; Wasef Alhroub
abstract: Childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis is rare, and its early picture is often too vague to point at a large-vessel vasculitis. We report a 12-year-old girl who presented with 13 days of recurrent severe retrosternal chest pain and diffuse colicky abdominal pain, on a background of six months of exertional fatigue and painful swelling of the right fingertips, without fever, weight loss or night sweats. Examination showed bilateral digital clubbing, a right arm blood pressure below the 5th percentile with left arm and lower limb readings between the 50th and 90th percentiles, an absent right radial pulse, and weak brachial and right posterior tibial pulses. The erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 110 mm/h and C-reactive protein 82 to 93 mg/L. Computed tomography angiography showed mild concentric mural thickening of the aortic arch with severe stenosis of the right common and internal carotid arteries, near-occlusion of the right subclavian artery, moderate to severe brachiocephalic stenosis, moderate narrowing of the left common carotid and left subclavian arteries, and moderate stenosis of the right common and superficial femoral arteries. The abdominal aorta and its visceral branches were spared. She met the EULAR/PRINTO/PRES (Ankara 2008) classification criteria for childhood Takayasu arteritis, and the arterial distribution corresponds to Numano type IIa, together with peripheral lower-limb involvement that the Numano scheme does not cover. Disease progressed on intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, methotrexate, aspirin and low-molecular-weight heparin, culminating in an 80% stenosis of the right common femoral artery. Adalimumab was started and later replaced by tocilizumab, after which the femoral peri-arterial inflammatory changes resolved on imaging and acute-phase reactants normalized. Blood pressure asymmetry, pulse deficits and the established stenoses persisted. This case suggests that normal inflammatory markers in childhood-onset Takayasu arteritis can coexist with fixed arterial damage, and that judgements about disease activity are better based on clinical findings and serial imaging together than on acute-phase reactants alone.

title: Transient Myocardial Ischemia and Coronary Vasospasm Precipitated by Non-Ionic Iodinated Contrast Media: A Case Report of Type I Kounis Syndrome
authors: Anak Agung Ngurah Satya Pranata; Ketut Suardamana; Dekta Filantropi Esa
abstract: Background: Intravenous iodinated contrast media can trigger life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions and acute coronary events through mast cell degranulation, termed Kounis syndrome. Type I Kounis syndrome entails coronary artery vasospasm in patients without pre-existing coronary artery disease. Objective: To describe the clinical course, recovery trajectories, and management of Type I Kounis syndrome after non-ionic contrast media in an atopic patient. Methods: A 41-year-old atopic woman developed severe dyspnea, diffuse bronchospasm, unmeasurable blood pressure, and hypoxemia (SpO2 88%) within minutes of intravenous iopromide 300 (20 mL) during cholangiography. She was followed at four milestones (T0, acute collapse; T1, 1 h after epinephrine; T2, 24 h; T3, 72 h) with serial 12-lead electrocardiography, arterial blood gas, point-of-care cardiopulmonary ultrasound, and transthoracic echocardiography. Values are reported descriptively. Results: At T0 the electrocardiogram showed sinus tachycardia (122 beats/min), diffuse T-wave inversion in V1–V5, and QTc 556 ms; lactate was 5.99 mmol/L and base deficit -6.0 mmol/L. Intramuscular epinephrine (0.5 mg, 1:1,000) with crystalloid fluid was followed by hemodynamic stabilization (mean arterial pressure 26.7 to 84.0 mmHg, +214.6%) and normalization of repolarization (QTc 418 ms, -24.8%). High-sensitivity troponin T stayed below the 99th percentile (<14.0 ng/L). Echocardiography showed ejection fraction 56%, no regional wall motion abnormality, and TAPSE 2.4 cm. The Naranjo score was 8/10, a probable adverse drug reaction. Conclusions: In this atopic patient, non-ionic contrast media were followed by transient repolarization abnormalities in keeping with Type I Kounis syndrome. Prompt intramuscular epinephrine was followed by recovery without evidence of worsening ischemia.

title: Anatomical Variations of Renal Arteries: Clinical, Radiological, and SurgicalConsiderations
authors: Evangelos Rodinos; Dimosthenis Chrysikos; Theodore G. Troupis
abstract: Objective. To synthesize the current knowledge regarding the embryological basis, anatomical classification, imaging characterization, and clinical implications of accessory renal arteries. Background. Anatomical variations in the renal arteries are common, affecting approximately 20-35% of the population, and have significant implications for clinical outcomes and surgical planning. Accessory renal arteries are usually terminal vessels that serve discrete renal islands with minimal collateral circulation in the body; therefore, their preoperative identification is important. However, there has been no modern synthesis of embryology, imaging, and multidisciplinary clinical treatment for these variations. Methods. A narrative review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar for publications from December 2015 to December 2025. MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to “accessory renal artery,” “multiple renal arteries,” “renal artery variations,” “renal vascular anatomy,” “kidney transplantation,” “renovascular hypertension,” “computed tomography angiography,” “magnetic resonance angiography,” and “endovascular aortic repair” were used in Boolean combinations. Peer-reviewed original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and case series were included. Conference abstracts, unpublished data, and non-English publications were excluded. Discussion. This review addresses the embryological basis and anatomical classification of accessory renal arteries; the diagnostic roles of Doppler ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography; and their clinical implications in kidney transplantation, partial nephrectomy, and endovascular aortic repair, including the contested association with renovascular hypertension. Available data suggest that most accessory vessels do not independently cause hypertension, whereas stenosis of larger vessels may be a correctable etiology in selected cases. Conclusion. Accessory renal arteries have a significant clinical impact, primarily determined by the size of the vessels and the area of the kidney they supply. Preoperative characterization based on modern imaging can be reliable and can help plan and manage surgery for each patient. More prospective research is required to establish evidence-based principles for vessel maintenance and evaluate new technologies in this context.

title: Sex differences in clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a real-world cohort
authors: Miriam Estévez Táboas; Julio Echarte‐Morales; Ernesto Ruiz Golcher; Carlos Eduardo Sotomayor-Casillas; André González García; David Neuhalfen; Carla Iglesias-Otero; Elena García-Campos Losada; Nazaret Vázquez-Vázquez; David González Fernández; Hugo Prado Prado; Carmen Cuiñas Fariña; Andrés Antelo-Abeijón; Pablo Juan‐Salvadores; Rodrigo Estévez‐Loureiro; Jose A. Baz Alonso; Andrés Íñiguez; Victor Alfonso Jímenez-Díaz
abstract: Background Severe aortic stenosis is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases in the ageing population, and transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has become an effective and less invasive therapeutic alternative. Anatomical, pathophysiological, and clinical differences between women and men may influence outcomes following the procedure. This study aimed to evaluate the association between sex and mortality and procedure-related complications after TAVI in a real-world cohort from the Vigo Health Area. Methods We conducted a retrospective, single-center observational study including 1,065 patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent transfemoral TAVI between 2010 and 2023. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality at 1 year. Secondary endpoints included bleeding, vascular complications, and new permanent pacemaker implantation. Time-to-event analyses were censored at 365 days; multivariable models used complete-case analysis. Results Women were older and had greater frailty and higher surgical risk scores than men. In-hospital and 1-year mortality were similar between sexes. Date-based 30-day mortality was 2.4% in men and 3.7% in women ( p = 0.225), and female sex was not independently associated with 30-day mortality after adjustment for age and STS score (adjusted OR 1.79, 95% CI 0.80–3.98; p = 0.154). Female sex was not independently associated with 1-year mortality (adjusted HR 1.07, 95% CI 0.69–1.66; p = 0.772). Women had more bleeding in unadjusted analyses, but female sex was not significantly associated with any bleeding after adjustment (adjusted OR 1.61, 95% CI 0.92–2.81; p = 0.093). Male sex remained associated with higher odds of new permanent pacemaker implantation (adjusted OR 1.49, 95% CI 1.03–2.17; p = 0.036). Conclusions Sex was not independently associated with short- or 1-year mortality after TAVI. Women had a higher unadjusted incidence of bleeding, whereas men had a higher incidence of new permanent pacemaker implantation that persisted after adjustment. These findings describe sex-related differences in procedural risk profiles but should be interpreted in the context of the observational design and the long study period.

title: Association between estimated glucose disposal rate and subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden in non-diabetic middle-aged and older adults
authors: Lei Guo; 赵玉波; Meng Qu; Ming Li; Jianchun Zhu; Sha Zheng; Jun Zhang
abstract: Objective To evaluate the association and dose–response relationship between estimated glucose disposal rate (eGDR), a surrogate marker of insulin resistance, and subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden in non-diabetic middle-aged and older adults. Methods This retrospective analysis used data from a prospective registry and included 604 adults aged ≥45 years without diabetes. Participants with symptomatic cerebrovascular disease, including prior ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack attributable to cerebrovascular stenosis, were excluded. Cerebrovascular atherosclerosis was assessed using carotid duplex ultrasonography, head and neck magnetic resonance angiography, or head and neck computed tomography angiography. Based on neuroimaging results, participants were classified into three categories: no atherosclerosis, single vascular bed involvement, and dual vascular bed involvement. Associations between eGDR and atherosclerotic burden were evaluated using ordinal logistic regression models, including unadjusted, age- and sex-adjusted, and fully adjusted models. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was performed to examine the dose–response relationship. Results All 604 participants were community-dwelling adults without symptomatic cerebrovascular disease. The mean age was 64 ± 11 years, and 220 (36.4%) were male. Participants with a higher subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden were older, had a higher prevalence of hypertension, and had lower eGDR levels ( p < 0.001). The prevalence of single and dual vascular bed involvement decreased progressively across eGDR quartiles, from the lowest (Q1) to the highest (Q4) quartile (single bed: 33.1% vs. 19.2%; dual beds: 13.2% vs. 2.0%). In the fully adjusted ordinal logistic regression model, each 1-SD increase in eGDR was associated with lower odds of being in a higher atherosclerotic burden category (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.62–0.89, p = 0.001). Compared with Q1, participants in Q4 had lower odds of being in a higher burden category (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.24–0.72, p = 0.001; P for trend = 0.002). The RCS analysis showed a linear correlation between eGDR and atherosclerotic burden (overall p = 0.002, non-linear p = 0.322). Conclusion Among middle-aged and older adults without diabetes, lower eGDR was independently associated with a higher subclinical cerebrovascular atherosclerotic burden, with a linear pattern. These findings warrant further investigation in prospective studies.

title: Complex antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes
authors: Bence Hegyi; Donald M. Bers
abstract: Introduction Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve clinical outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) and may reduce sudden cardiac death; however, the underlying antiarrhythmic mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Methods We investigated the cellular electrophysiological effects of the SGLT2 inhibitor empagliflozin in isolated cardiomyocytes from two non-ischemic, non-diabetic HFrEF models (rabbit and mouse). Results Ventricular cardiomyocytes from both HFrEF models exhibited prolonged action potential duration (APD), increased short-term APD variability (STV), and greater susceptibility to APD alternans and delayed afterdepolarizations (DADs). Intracellular Ca2+ buffering with EGTA prevented DADs, attenuated APD prolongation, and reduced repolarization instability. HFrEF cardiomyocytes also showed enhanced late Na+ current (INa,L) and reduced inward rectifier K+ current (IK1). Cell pretreatment with empagliflozin (1 μmol/L, 3 h), but not acute application (3 min), attenuated proarrhythmogenic AP changes, reduced INa,L, and increased IK1 in both species. Empagliflozin had no significant electrophysiological effects in healthy control cardiomyocytes. Selective inhibition of Na+/H+ exchanger-1 (NHE-1) with cariporide (1 μmol/L, 3 h) failed to reproduce the antiarrhythmic effects of empagliflozin under our experimental conditions; however, our studies were performed with intracellular pH buffered to 7.2, where NHE-1 activity is low. Discussion These results demonstrate that empagliflozin attenuates key proarrhythmic electrophysiological changes in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes. The requirement for drug pretreatment supports the hypothesis that empagliflozin acts through modulation of ion channel functional expression and/or post-translational regulation rather than direct acute channel effects in non-ischemic HFrEF cardiomyocytes.

title: Totally endoscopic mitral valve replacement: reasons for non-feasibility of repair and 5-year outcomes
authors: Friedrich Sobik; Jonas Pausch; Xiaoqin Hua; Martin Beyer; Evelina Macius; Oliver Daniel Bhadra; Y. Alassar; Benjamin Kloth; Lenard Conradi; Hermann C. Reichenspurner; Simon Pecha; E. Girdauskas; Andreas Schaefer
abstract: Objectives Totally endoscopic mitral valve (MV) surgery is an established therapy for mitral regurgitation (MR) with high repair rates at experienced centers. In certain scenarios, however, repair is not feasible, necessitating chordal-sparing MV replacement. This study investigates the reasons for totally endoscopic MV replacement and reports 5-year outcomes. Methods Between 2012 and 2022, 1,037 consecutive patients underwent totally endoscopic MV surgery. Of those, 75 patients (7.2%) underwent chordal-sparing MV replacement. Preoperative characteristics, periprocedural data, and mid-term outcomes were retrospectively analyzed and compared to a 1:1 propensity score-matched repair group. Results After matching, baseline characteristics were balanced. Indications for MV replacement included sclerotic leaflets (28.0%), endocarditis (26.7%), MV stenosis (17.3%), failed repair attempt (17.3%), rheumatic disease (12.0%), and residual MR after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (7%). Cross-clamp and bypass times were similar. Re-thoracotomy occurred in 14.7% vs. 6.7%, while permanent pacemaker implantation occurred solely after replacement (16.0%). Low cardiac output rates were comparable (6.7% vs. 5.5%). Transvalvular gradients at discharge were higher after replacement ( p < 0.001). No paravalvular leakage was observed. In-hospital mortality was 4% vs. 0%. Five-year survival was 86.7% vs. 94.7%, and reintervention rates were similar (4.0% vs. 6.7%). Conclusion Totally endoscopic MV surgery at a high-volume center is infrequently associated with MV replacement. The main reasons included sclerotic leaflet pathology, MV stenosis, and endocarditis. Despite a higher comorbidity burden and residual baseline imbalance after matching, early and mid-term outcomes were acceptable. Totally endoscopic chordal-sparing MV replacement represents a safe and clinically effective treatment option for selected patients.

title: Imaging-derived coronary fractional flow reserve: advances in physics-based, machine learning, and physics-informed methods
authors: Tanxin Zhu; Emran Hossen; Chen Zhao; Jingfeng Jiang; Michele Esposito; Jiguang Sun; Weihua Zhou
abstract: Purpose of Review Imaging-derived fractional flow reserve (FFR) is rapidly evolving beyond conventional computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-based pipelines toward machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and physics-informed approaches that enable fast, wire-free, and scalable functional assessment of coronary artery stenosis. This review synthesizes recent advances in computed tomography (CT)-and angiography-based FFR measurement, with particular emphasis on emerging physics-informed neural networks and neural operators (PINNs and PINOs), as well as key considerations for their clinical translation.Recent Findings ML/DL approaches have markedly improved automation and computational speed, enabling prediction of pressure and FFR from anatomical descriptors or angiographic contrast dynamics. However, their real-world performance and generalizability can remain variable and sensitive to domain shift, due to multi-center heterogeneity, interpretability challenges, and differences in acquisition protocols and image quality. Physics-informed learning introduces conservation structure and boundary-condition consistency into model training, improving generalizability and reducing dependence on dense supervision while maintaining rapid inference. Recent evaluation trends increasingly highlight deployment-oriented metrics, including calibration, uncertainty quantification, and quality-control gatekeeping, as essential for safe clinical use.SummaryThe field is converging toward imaging-derived FFR methods that are faster, more automated, and more reliable. While ML/DL offers substantial efficiency gains, physics-informed frameworks such as PINNs and PINOs may provide a more robust balance between speed and physical consistency. Prospective multi-center validation and standardized evaluation will be critical to support broad and safe clinical adoption.

title: Recent achievements of the National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) bioresources through Japanese fiscal year 2025
authors: Yosuke Omae; Katsushi Tokunaga
abstract: The National Center Biobank Network (NCBN) is constituted by a network of biobanks from five National Centers and the Japan Institute for Health Security (JIHS). The NCBN primarily collects samples from patients with various diseases, amassing a total of more than 250,000 participants and 800,000 human biospecimens as of the end of March 2026. The primary sample types are blood and DNA, with spinal fluid and frozen tissue samples also collected depending on the characteristics of the disease. These samples are accompanied by highly specialized and traceable clinical information supported by advanced medical care and expertise. Moreover, some samples are accompanied by whole-genome sequencing data. Consequently, these resources provide a unique platform for translational research, biomarker discovery, and genomic medicine in Japan. In the present review, we provide a detailed account of the recent achievements of NCBN biobanks and their biospecimens and genomic data.

title: Impacto da correção da estenose aórtica no ressangramento em pacientes com Síndrome de Heyde: revisão sistemática com metanálise
authors: João Paulo Ferreira Andrade; Maria Eduarda Ferreira de Andrade; Ana Carolina Ribeiro de Carvalho; Pedro de Medeiros Chaves Bisneto; Leda Maria Delmondes Freitas Trindade
abstract: A Síndrome de Heyde (SH) caracteriza-se pela associação entre estenose aórtica (EA), coagulopatia adquirida e sangramento gastrointestinal relacionado a angiodisplasias. Embora a substituição valvar atue sobre os mecanismos fisiopatológicos da doença, persistem divergências quanto ao controle hemorrágico após a intervenção. Este estudo objetivou avaliar a ocorrência de sangramento gastrointestinal após a correção da EA por implante transcateter de valva aórtica (TAVI) ou substituição cirúrgica da valva aórtica (SAVR), bem como sintetizar os desfechos hematológicos, transfusionais e endoscópicos. Trata-se de uma revisão sistemática com metanálise, conduzida conforme as recomendações PRISMA, com buscas nas bases PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase e SciELO entre janeiro e março de 2026. Foram incluídos estudos com pacientes com EA associada a sangramento gastrointestinal e/ou angiodisplasia que reportaram desfechos após intervenção valvar. O desfecho primário foi o ressangramento gastrointestinal, enquanto os secundários compreenderam os níveis de hemoglobina, a necessidade transfusional e as características endoscópicas. Dos 358 registros identificados, 11 estudos foram incluídos, sendo seis elegíveis para metanálise. Os estudos reportaram 1.579 pacientes, com idade média entre 74 e 80,7 anos. A taxa global de ressangramento após substituição valvar foi de 25% (IC95%: 21%–30%; I²=37%), considerando 355 pacientes. Observou-se aumento da hemoglobina de 0,96 g/dL (IC95%: 0,43–1,49; I²=0%), além de redução da necessidade transfusional e da carga de lesões angiodisplásicas. Conclui-se que a substituição valvar esteve associada a desfechos hemorrágicos favoráveis, com aproximadamente 75% dos pacientes livres de novos episódios de sangramento durante o seguimento. Entretanto, a recorrência hemorrágica persistiu em parte dos pacientes, possivelmente associada à doença valvar residual, ao vazamento paravalvar e à persistência das angiodisplasias. Não foi possível estabelecer superioridade definitiva entre TAVI e SAVR quanto ao controle hemorrágico.

title: The gut-brain-vascular axis: converging neuroinflammatory and hypertension-mediated pathways from gut dysbiosis to cognitive decline
authors: Shaurya Mehta; Pranav Loomba; Hamoudi Musselmani; Jaret Ly; Sami Nguyen; Alex Niemann; Sree Kolli; David Sant
abstract: Hypertension and cognitive decline are major public health burdens, and both have been associated with gut microbiome dysbiosis. We propose the gut-brain-vascular axis as a testable synthesis in which dysbiosis may contribute to cognitive decline through two converging routes: direct neuroinflammatory signaling and hypertension-mediated cerebrovascular injury. In the proposed direct route, intestinal barrier dysfunction, lipopolysaccharide translocation, altered microbial metabolites, microglial activation, and vagal signaling may promote neuroinflammation. In the indirect route, dysbiosis-associated metabolites, immune activation, autonomic imbalance, and endothelial injury may contribute to hypertension, which is linked to cerebral small vessel disease, impaired cerebral autoregulation, neurovascular uncoupling, and blood-brain barrier dysfunction. The component relationships are supported to different degrees, but the complete temporal pathway and an interaction between the two routes have not been established in humans. This narrative review synthesizes gut-hypertension, gut-cognitive, cerebrovascular, shared-mechanism, and therapeutic evidence and identifies the study designs needed to test the framework. Longitudinal cohorts and trials that measure microbiome, blood pressure, cerebrovascular, and cognitive outcomes together are required to determine whether the proposed routes occur independently, sequentially, or interactively.

title: Association of lipoprotein(a) with ischemia–reperfusion injury in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction
authors: Magdalena Holzknecht; Christina Tiller; Ivan Lechner; Fritz Oberhollenzer; Alex Kaser; Philipp Fischer; Anita Sandor; Can Gollmann‐Tepeköylü; Agnes Mayr; Axel Bauer; Bernhard Metzler; Sebastian J. Reinstadler; Martin Reindl
abstract: Abstract Background Hypercholesterolemia adversely affects ischemia–reperfusion injury in acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) is an independent cardiovascular risk factor beyond traditional lipid markers; however, its impact on ischemic myocardial injury remains unclear. We therefore investigated the association of Lp(a) with myocardial and microvascular damage assessed by multiparametric cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR), as well as clinical outcomes in STEMI patients. Methods and Results In this prospective MARINA-STEMI (NCT04113356) cohort study, 518 STEMI patients (median age 59 years, 19% female) treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) were included. Lp(a) and lipid parameters, including low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, were measured at hospital admission. CMR was performed at a median of 4 days (interquartile range (IQR) 3–5) and 4 months (IQR 4–5) after PCI. The primary objective was to assess the association of Lp(a) with infarct size (IS) and severe microvascular injury, defined as intramyocardial hemorrhage (IMH) on baseline CMR. The clinical endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: all-cause death, re-infarction, or new congestive heart failure). Median Lp(a) and LDL cholesterol levels were 27 nmol/l (IQR 20–90) and 141 mg/dl (IQR 117–166), respectively. LDL cholesterol correlated with IS at baseline ( ρ = 0.114, p = 0.010) and was higher in patients with IMH (145 vs. 140 mg/dl, p = 0.031). In contrast, Lp(a) showed no correlation with IS ( ρ = 0.051, p = 0.246) and no association with IMH (25 vs. 28 nmol/l, p = 0.632). Elevated Lp(a) (≥ 105 nmol/l) was not associated with MACE (8.7% vs. 8.8%, p = 0.966). Conclusions While LDL cholesterol was significantly associated with IS and IMH, Lp(a) was not related to ischemia–reperfusion injury patterns or clinical outcomes in patients with STEMI treated with primary PCI. Lp(a) concentrations ≥ 105 nmol/l are considered elevated according to current guidelines [1]. CMR = cardiovascular magnetic resonance; IMH = intramyocardial hemorrhage; IS = infarct size; LDL = low-density lipoprotein cholesterol; Lp(a) = lipoprotein(a); LVMM = left ventricular myocardial mass; MACE = major adverse cardiovascular events; pPCI = primary percutaneous coronary intervention; STEMI = ST-elevation myocardial infarction.

title: Immune-driven remodeling in calcific aortic valve disease: mechanisms and immunotherapeutic opportunities
authors: Xi Zhang; Yi Si; Ling Liao; Yuxiang Wu
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a prevalent degenerative valvular disorder in the aging population, for which no pharmacological therapy has proven effective in halting or reversing disease progression. Over the past decade, CAVD has been increasingly recognized not as a passive degenerative process of calcium deposition, but as an active, inflammation-driven disease characterized by osteogenic remodeling. This process is initiated and sustained by endothelial injury, lipid retention, immune cell infiltration, and phenotypic transition of valvular interstitial cells. Growing evidence indicates that innate and adaptive immune responses may contribute to disease amplification. Innate immune cells propagate local inflammatory signaling through inflammasome activation, extracellular vesicle communication, protease release, and neutrophil extracellular trap formation, while adaptive immune cells further shape disease progression by sustaining cytokine networks that promote fibrosis and osteogenic reprogramming within the valvular microenvironment. Based on these mechanistic insights, this review further discusses emerging translational strategies aimed at targeting key pathogenic processes in CAVD, including modulation of inflammatory signaling, restoration of adaptive immune homeostasis, regulation of extracellular matrix remodeling and antifibrotic pathways, inhibition of VIC osteogenic differentiation, as well as development of patient stratification and local drug delivery approaches. Collectively, these strategies may provide a conceptual framework for earlier, non-surgical interventions for CAVD.

title: Factores Sociodemograficos, Estado Nutricional y Carga Comórbida en Adultos Mayores de Buenavista, Ecuador, 2025
authors: Francine Maribel Rodriguez Diaz; Jennifer Nicole Gonzaga Aguilar; Elizabeth Miranda Velázquez
abstract: Objetivo: Analizar las características sociodemográficas, el estado nutricional y la carga comórbida en adultos mayores atendidos en la parroquia rural Buenavista, cantón Pasaje, a partir del censo de historias clínicas del periodo 2025-D2. Métodos: Estudio observacional, descriptivo, transversal y retrospectivo. La población accesible comprendió la totalidad de las 111 historias clínicas elegibles del proyecto institucional "Vivir con plenitud: mejorando la salud en la edad de oro" (diseño censal, sin muestreo). Se recolectaron variables sociodemográficas (sexo, edad, nivel de instrucción, tipología familiar), antropométricas (IMC según criterios de la OMS, ICC para distribución androide) y la carga comórbida ponderada calculada mediante el Índice de Comorbilidad de Charlson (ICC). El análisis estadístico empleó frecuencias absolutas, porcentajes, medias y desviaciones estándar. Resultados: La media de edad fue de 75,47 ± 6,60 años, con predominio del sexo femenino (57,7 %). El 64,0 % presentó escolaridad primaria o nula y el 31,5 % residía en hogares monoparentales o unipersonales. La evaluación antropométrica mostró un IMC medio de 28,42 ± 5,12 kg/m², clasificando obesidad en el 32,4 % y sobrepeso en el 30,6 %. Por el contrario, el ICC arrojó una media de 0,96 ± 0,08, ubicando al 78,4 % en riesgo metabólico alto. El Índice de Charlson presentó una media de 1,13 ± 0,94 puntos; el 29,7 % de los pacientes exhibió una puntuación ≥2 (carga comórbida moderada o alta). Las enfermedades crónicas más reportadas fueron hipertensión arterial (58,6 %) y diabetes mellitus tipo 2 (24,3 %). Conclusiones: La población evaluada exhibe una sustancial vulnerabilidad sociodemográfica, una alta frecuencia de adiposidad central estimada por ICC y una notable concentración de comorbilidad vascular y disglucémica. El diseño descriptivo no permite establecer correlaciones ni inferencias predictivas o de causalidad.

title: HRC Research Day 2026
abstract: Psychiatry in Malaysia is expanding within a complex training ecosystem that includes university pathways, service-based Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH) training, and the MRCPsych parallel pathway, yet it still lacks a dedicated college under the Academy of Medicine of Malaysia (AMM).This study examined whether regional psychiatry college models and Malaysian workforce evidence support the case for such a platform.A structured narrative comparative review was conducted using bibliographic sources, official institutional websites, targeted Google site-specific searches, and citation tracking.Included sources were organised into a comparative framework matrix and synthesised thematically across governance, training, credentialing, continuing professional development, standards, advocacy, professional identity and international linkage.The review included 11 regional institutional sources and 3 Malaysian contextual documents or data sources.Regional models differed in structure but converged in key functions including training support, credentialing, continuing professional development, standards work, advocacy, professional identity, and selective international linkage.Official Malaysian data identified 111 current pathwaylinked psychiatrists and 445 psychiatrists in MOH settings, indicating that the pathway-linked cohort constituted approximately 24.9% of the MOH psychiatry workforce.Regional psychiatry bodies differ in form but converge in function.Malaysia now has a visible and institutionally relevant psychiatry constituency, suggesting that a future College of Psychiatrists under AMM may be timely as a durable academic-professional platform to strengthen specialty development, rather than as a parallel regulator.
