title: Fatal Cardiopulmonary Collapse, Bilateral Pleural Effusion, and Hypoxic En-cephalopathy in Neglected Severe Preeclampsia: A Case Report on Antenatal Surveillance and Access Gaps
authors: Yohanes Adam Elsoin
journal: Sriwijaya Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
abstract: Background: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal death worldwide. Where antenatal care (ANC) is absent and women lack health insurance, a hypertensive crisis can progress quickly to fatal multi-organ failure. Objective: To describe the clinical, hemodynamic, and laboratory course of fatal postpartum cardiopulmonary collapse after unmonitored severe preeclampsia. Methods: Single-patient case report (CARE guideline) at Dr. Saiful Anwar General Hospital, Malang, Indonesia. Clinical findings, serial laboratory values, arterial blood gases, echocardiography, ultrasonography, and chest radiography were recorded over nine days of intensive care and presented chronologically, with a descriptive comparison with the literature. Results: A 44-year-old uninsured primiparous woman with no ANC contacts had an emergency cesarean delivery for severe preeclampsia and left a secondary hospital against medical advice on postoperative day 2 because of financial hardship. At tertiary admission she was obtunded (Glasgow Coma Scale 13), with blood pressure 166/94 mmHg, hemoglobin 5.5 g/dL, and oliguria. Radiography showed large asymmetric bilateral pleural effusions (left ~1,250 mL) with compressive atelectasis; PaO₂/FiO₂ was 142.1 mmHg. Echocardiography showed concentric left ventricular hypertrophy, systemic vascular resistance 2,140 dyn·s/cm⁵, and E/e' 17.8 (PCWP ~24 mmHg). Despite mechanical ventilation, nicardipine, transfusions, and albumin, anuric renal failure (creatinine 5.20 mg/dL) and severe acidosis (pH 7.08, lactate 11.4 mmol/L) progressed, and cardiopulmonary arrest occurred on day 9. Conclusion: In this patient, unmonitored severe preeclampsia was followed by fatal cardiopulmonary collapse; hydrostatic overload and endothelial hyperpermeability are proposed mechanisms that were not directly measured. Emergency coverage at private obstetric facilities may help prevent premature discharge.

title: Ultrasound-guided haemodynamic profiling in haemodialysis patients: a single-centre prospective observational study protocol
authors: Samuel Larsen; Fabio Silvio Taccone; Alaín Le Moine; Filippo Annoni; Thomas E.R. Baudoux
abstract: Background Intradialytic hypotension (IDH) and chronic fluid overload are common and clinically important complications of maintenance haemodialysis, yet routine volume assessment remains imprecise. Multi-organ point-of-care ultrasound may provide a structured bedside assessment of cardiac reserve, pulmonary congestion and venous congestion. Methods and analysis This single-centre prospective observational cohort study will enrol approximately 60 adult patients receiving maintenance haemodialysis. Participants will undergo integrated ultrasound profiling immediately before and after dialysis at baseline and at 3, 6 and 9 months, with clinical outcomes followed for 12 months. The ultrasound protocol includes focused cardiac ultrasound, eight-zone lung ultrasound B-line quantification and a modified VEXUS assessment using inferior vena cava, hepatic vein and portal vein findings. Event-triggered intradialytic scans may also be performed for current IDH or suspected mismatch between the prescribed target weight and the best clinically tolerated weight. These examinations will not be pooled with scheduled assessments. A separate exploratory post-scan association analysis will include only scans completed while the patient is clinically stable, before the first same-session IDH and not in response to evolving current-session haemodynamic instability; the outcome is subsequent IDH before session end. Scans obtained during or after IDH or during evolving instability will be described only. The main descriptive objective is to characterise pre- and post-dialysis ultrasound-derived haemodynamic profiles and their within-session and longitudinal variability. The primary prespecified analysis for Objective 2 is an exploratory and non-confirmatory assessment of the within-patient association between pre-dialysis ultrasound parameters and same-session IDH using a scheduled-session case-crossover design. Secondary analyses include the separate event-triggered post-scan association analysis and an exploratory scheduled-session mixed-effects analysis. Event-triggered examinations will not contribute cases to the primary analysis. Exploratory objectives assess clinician-perceived usefulness and documented clinician-implemented prescription changes after delayed disclosure, without assessing clinical benefit. Ethics and dissemination The study has received ethics approval and will be conducted after written informed consent. Results will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications and scientific meetings. Study registration https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN80571205 , identifier ISRCTN80571205.

title: Cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes: insights from myocardial strain and renal Doppler assessment
authors: Ahmed Atef; Ahmed Fayed; Hemmat El- Haddad; Moataz Fathy; Heba El Deeb
abstract: Prediabetes and early type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) may be accompanied by subclinical cardiac and renal injury before overt disease appears. This study evaluated early cardio-renal dysfunction in prediabetes and early T2DM using myocardial strain imaging and renal Doppler assessment. This cross-sectional study included 180 participants: 60 with prediabetes, 60 with newly diagnosed T2DM (≤ 2 years), and 60 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Conventional echocardiography and two-dimensional speckle-tracking echocardiography were used to assess left ventricular (LV) function and left atrial (LA) mechanics. Renal vascular resistance was assessed using the Doppler-derived renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI). Glycemic status and albuminuria were evaluated using fasting glucose, oral glucose tolerance testing, HbA1c, and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio. Compared with controls, participants with prediabetes and T2DM showed early alterations in LV relaxation/filling indices and reduced LA strain. LV ejection fraction was modestly lower, while GLS became progressively less negative across the dysglycemic groups ( p < 0.001), consistent with reduced longitudinal myocardial deformation. Renal resistive index (RRI) and pulsatility index (PI) were significantly increased in the dysglycemic groups. RRI correlated positively with E/e′, linking higher renal vascular resistance with higher estimated LV filling pressure ( r = 0.440, p < 0.001). Prediabetes and early T2DM were associated with subclinical abnormalities in myocardial mechanics and renal vascular indices despite preserved conventional cardiac and renal function. Myocardial strain and renal Doppler measures may provide complementary phenotypic information, but prospective validation is required before routine clinical application.

title: Case Report: Twelve-year longitudinal CMR follow-up in Becker muscular dystrophy–associated cardiomyopathy
authors: Mohd Imree Azmi; Masafumi Takafuji; Sven Plein
abstract: Cardiac involvement is an important cause of morbidity and mortality in Becker muscular dystrophy. Myocardial disease may progress despite relatively limited findings on conventional echocardiography, while cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) provides detailed assessment of ventricular function and myocardial tissue characteristics with late gadolinium enhancement (LGE), parametric mapping and strain analysis. We report a case of 57 year-old man with genetically confirmed Becker muscular dystrophy who underwent CMR examinations 12 years apart. Follow-up imaging demonstrated progressive left ventricular remodelling, a decline in left ventricular ejection fraction and interval changes in the distribution and extent of myocardial fibrosis. This case provides a long-term within-patient comparison of Becker muscular dystrophy associated cardiomyopathy and illustrates the additional information provided by serial CMR in documenting progressive myocardial involvement over time.

title: Investigation of the relationship between heart rate measured automatically at different time intervals using the 3M littmann 3200 electronic stethoscope and heart rate measured by electrocardiography
authors: Ömer Aydın
journal: Journal of Advances in VetBio Science and Techniques
abstract: Cardiac auscultation is an indispensable method in the examination of cats. With a traditional stethoscope, heart murmurs, gallop rhythms, and heart rate (HR) may not always be accurately assessed because of ambient noise interference. However, electronic stethoscopes (ESs) provide more uniform and amplified acoustic signals, allowing more accurate identification of physiological and pathological heart sounds during auscultation. The aim of this study was to determine the agreement, differences, and correlation between HR automatically measured using a 3M Littmann 3200 ES over 15-, 30-, and 60-second intervals and HR obtained by electrocardiography (ECG) in 34 healthy cats of various breeds, ages, and sexes. To this end, intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC), Bland–Altman, and Spearman’s correlation analyses were performed. ICC analysis showed moderate agreement between ECG and ES at the 15- and 60-second measurement intervals (r = 0.661, P < 0.001; r = 0.700, P < 0.001, respectively), whereas the 30-second interval demonstrated higher agreement (r = 0.812, P < 0.001). According to Bland-Altman analysis, 30-second HR measurements by ES showed the closest agreement with ECG (bias = 5.03; 95% limits of agreement = -34.34 to 44.40), compared to 15 seconds (bias = 9.41; -48.34 to 67.16) and 60 seconds (bias = 9.06; -41.88 to 59.99). In conclusion, this study demonstrates that 30-second measurements obtained with the 3M Littmann 3200 ES provide heart rate measurements comparable to those obtained by ECG in healthy cats.

title: HEART Score as a Predictor of Angiographic Severity of Coronary Artery Disease in Patients Diagnosed with Acute Coronary Syndrome
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide.Rapid risk stratification of patients presenting with chest pain is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate management.The HEART score, which incorporates History, Electrocardiogram, Age, Risk factors, and Troponin levels, has emerged as a simple and effective clinical tool for predicting major adverse cardiac events.However, limited studies have evaluated its relationship with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease (CAD), particularly in the Indian population.Objective: To assess the HEART score in patients with acute coronary syndrome and to evaluate its correlation with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease.Methods: This prospective observational study was conducted in the Department of General Medicine at a tertiary care teaching hospital.A total of 50 adult patients diagnosed with acute coronary syndrome were included.Clinical history, cardiovascular risk factors, electrocardiographic findings, and troponin levels were recorded, and the HEART score was calculated for each patient.Patients were categorized into low-risk (0-3), moderate-risk (4-6), and high-risk (7-10) groups.All patients underwent coronary angiography to determine the severity of coronary artery disease.Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software, and the association between HEART score categories and angiographic findings was analyzed using the Chi-square test, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant.Results: The mean age of the study population was 56.8 ± 11.4 years, and 68% of the patients were male.Hypertension (60%) and diabetes mellitus (52%) were the most common cardiovascular risk factors.Based on the HEART score classification, 18% of patients were categorized as low risk, 52% as moderate risk, and 30% as high risk.Coronary angiography revealed single vessel disease in 36% of patients, double vessel disease in 26%, triple vessel disease in 20%, and normal coronary arteries in 18%.A significant association was observed between increasing HEART score categories and the severity of coronary artery disease (χ² = 12.84, p = 0.002), with multi-vessel disease predominantly observed in patients with higher HEART scores. Conclusion:The HEART score is a simple and effective bedside risk stratification tool that correlates significantly with the angiographic severity of coronary artery disease in patients with acute coronary syndrome.Its routine use in clinical practice may help identify high-risk patients early and facilitate timely diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.

title: Isolated Disturbance of Consciousness as Initial Presentation of Staphylococcus aureus Endocarditis: A Case Report With Brief Literature Review
authors: Weixiong Zhong; 黄珊珊; Jing Jiang; Zhixu Tan
abstract: Objective:Challenging differential diagnosis Background:Infective endocarditis (IE) typically presents with fever, a heart murmur, or constitutional symptoms, making diagnosis challenging when neurological manifestations predominate.We report an atypical case of IE in which disturbance of consciousness was the initial manifestation. Case Report:A man in his 50s was admitted to our hospital with isolated disturbance of consciousness and no history of fever; a temperature of 38 °C was recorded on admission.Investigations confirmed an extensive acute right hemispheric watershed (border-zone) infarction involving the right temporoparietal lobe, without evidence of hemorrhagic transformation or intracranial hemorrhage.Subsequent workup identified Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, mitral valve vegetation, and multiple organ dysfunction syndrome.The absence of classic IE risk factors contributed to a delayed diagnosis.Guideline-concordant clinical management was implemented.Long-term outcome data were unavailable because of patient transfer; only in-hospital mortality (after transfer) was confirmed.We discuss the application of the 2023 Duke criteria to this case and examine factors contributing to the delayed diagnosis of IE.Disturbance of consciousness as the predominant initial manifestation of S. aureus IE is rare and frequently results in diagnostic delay.This case underscores the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for IE in patients with sepsis complicated by acute cerebral infarction, particularly among critical care and neurology clinicians. Conclusions:This case highlights isolated disturbance of consciousness as an atypical initial presentation of IE.Although IE is frequently complicated by acute cerebral infarction, clinicians may not routinely consider IE in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with disturbed consciousness.

title: Optimal timing of surgical intervention for post-myocardial infarction ventricular septal rupture: A comprehensive evidence review
authors: Irfan Rasheed; Mansyur Arif; Shyam Sunder Kolvekar
abstract: BackgroundVentricular septal rupture (VSR) is a rare but devastating complication of acute myocardial infarction, historically associated with extremely high mortality rates. The optimal timing of surgical repair-balancing the risks of operating on friable, acute necrosis against the dangers of progressive cardiogenic shock during a waiting period-remains a central clinical dilemma.MethodsA systematic narrative review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and Cochrane Library databases were searched from 2000 to 2024 for studies comparing early (≤7 days) versus delayed (>7 days) surgical repair of post-MI VSR. Data were extracted on patient characteristics, mechanical circulatory support (MCS) use, surgical techniques, and clinical outcomes, including operative mortality, reoperation rates, and long-term survival.ResultsEvidence from contemporary observational studies confirms that delayed surgical repair is associated with significantly lower operative mortality compared to early repair, primarily due to superior tissue integrity and lower rates of residual shunt. However, this mortality gap has substantially narrowed in the contemporary era with routine use of advanced MCS, particularly veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) and Impella devices. These technologies enable hemodynamic stabilization, transforming early repair from a salvage procedure to a more controlled intervention. Modern management has evolved from a rigid temporal dichotomy to a patient-tailored strategy emphasizing immediate stabilization, risk stratification, and selective MCS bridging to the optimal surgical window.ConclusionWhile delayed repair remains preferred for hemodynamically stable patients, early repair supported by advanced MCS represents a viable and often necessary strategy for patients with refractory shock. The decision paradigm has shifted toward "stabilize, support, then repair," requiring multidisciplinary heart team collaboration. Future directions include standardized MCS protocols, validated risk scores, and exploration of hybrid percutaneous-surgical approaches to further improve outcomes for this high-risk population.

title: Comparative genomics identifies a cyl-like region in Streptococcus sinensis isolates from a patient with infective endocarditis
authors: Wei Ma; Yanjun Zhang; 黄晓春; Yuxiang Wan; Changzi Deng; Jia Lin; Li Xu; Qin Qin
abstract: Streptococcus sinensis is an uncommon member of the viridans group streptococci reported in infective endocarditis (IE), but its genomic characteristics remain incompletely defined. We performed whole-genome sequencing of three S. sinensis isolates recovered from blood culture and valvular tissue from a single patient with IE and compared them with 199 public Streptococcus genomes. Orthology analysis, phylogenetic reconstruction, SNP analysis, VFDB and CARD screening, gene-specific BLAST, Pfam/HMMER analysis, read mapping, synteny comparison, in silico structural modeling, and erythrocyte hemolysis assays were integrated. The three isolates differed by only 0–1 SNPs and formed a near-clonal group. Core single-copy ortholog phylogeny placed S. sinensis closest to S. cristatus , followed by S. sanguinis and S. gordonii . The three isolates retained the host-interaction-associated genes eno , pavA , and plr / gapA and carried an identical 11,341-bp, 12-gene cyl -like block comprising 11 cyl -like genes and acpC . Core-gene phylogeny analysis indicated that the distribution of the complete block was lineage-associated. Gene-specific BLAST and read mapping confirmed full-length sequence conservation and complete mapped-base coverage of the block, while Pfam/HMMER supported enzyme- and transporter-associated domain assignments for several encoded proteins. Structural modeling predicted soluble enzyme-like folds for CylG-like and CylZ-like proteins and a membrane-permease-like architecture with transmembrane helices for CylB-like. On Columbia sheep-blood agar, all three clinical isolates showed visible hemolytic zones and exhibited detectable hemolytic activity in a sheep erythrocyte hemolysis assay. All three S. sinensis isolates shared a type 1 CARD-derived resistance-marker profile containing only Spne_parC_FLO . These findings clarify the phylogenomic position of the near-clonal clinical isolates and identify a shared cyl -like genomic region accompanied by measurable hemolytic activity, providing a basis for further investigation of their host-interaction and pathogenic potential.

title: Mitral valve repair for pediatric dilated cardiomyopathy with severe functional mitral regurgitation: a mechanism-anchored, proof-of-concept preoperative selection framework with supportive cohort and pooled outcomes
authors: Mete Han Kızılkaya; Boran Cakan; Aylin Ardali; Mehmet Biçer; Murat Tanyıldız; Ömer Özden; Ender Ödemiş
abstract: Functional mitral regurgitation (FMR) develops in 40–65% of children with dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and independently predicts death or transplantation. Published pediatric mitral valve repair (MVR) series from 2003 to 2024 report clinical stabilization rates of 0% to 100% and perioperative mortality of 0% to 50%. This heterogeneity is multifactorial, reflecting the surgical era, technique, institutional experience, patient acuity, and reporting standards, with patient selection being a contributing factor that has not yet been systematically examined. No preoperative framework currently exists to identify which children are most likely to benefit. A mechanism-anchored, three-category proof-of-concept clinical framework was defined a priori. Patients were classified as Non-MR-dominant if any of four affirmative features were documented (N1: toxic, storage, infiltrative, or myopathic etiology; N2: primary structural mitral valve disease; N3: preoperative irreversible end-organ failure or ECMO with multi-organ dysfunction; N4: severe RV dysfunction, fixed pulmonary hypertension, or severe tricuspid regurgitation from RV/annular dilatation). Patients without any N-feature who met three volume-overload criteria (idiopathic, familial, or sarcomeric DCM; functional MR ≥ 3+; LVEDd Pettersen Z-score ≥ + 5) were classified as MR-dominant. A Borderline MR-dominant category captured patients who did not meet all MR-dominant criteria but satisfied one of three predefined conditions (infancy with intermediate fractional shortening; post-myocarditis with documented regional scar or fibrotic substrate; or an LVEDd Pettersen Z-score of + 3.5 to < + 5 with severe functional MR). The framework was applied to a single-center cohort of six consecutive children and, masked to outcome, to all 22 previously published pediatric MVR-receiving patients. In the index cohort, three MR-dominant children underwent MVR and sustained remodeling, with transplant-free survival at a median 30-month follow-up and NT-proBNP reductions of 86–99%. Three children not selected for MVR (an MR-dominant child whose family declined surgery, and two Non-MR-dominant children) all died. In the pooled MVR-receiving cohort ( n = 25), MR-dominant plus Borderline patients achieved clinical stabilization and/or remodeling in 16/20 (80%) versus 1/5 (20%) Non-MR-dominant patients (Fisher exact p = 0.024; odds ratio 11.0, 95% CI 1.3–91.8). The association is statistically significant in the primary specification but is fragile to single-patient reclassification, an unavoidable consequence of reporting only five Non-MR-dominant patients across three decades of global pediatric literature. A fully preoperative, mechanism-anchored framework that places the burden of proof on Non-MR-dominant assignment offers a coherent, biologically grounded interpretation of three decades of heterogeneous pediatric MVR outcomes. In MR-dominant disease, MVR may support clinical stabilization with the potential for remodeling and may be a viable bridging or alternative strategy where transplantation and durable ventricular assist device support are inaccessible. The framework should be regarded as a proof-of-concept clinical hypothesis rather than a validated decision algorithm; prospective multicenter validation is required before clinical adoption.

title: Awareness as a path to inner strength: a qualitative study on women living with heart failure
authors: Federica Dellafiore; Serena Cazzato; Flavia Primosa; Lucia Gotri; Orejeta Diamanti; Gloria Maria Modena; Giovanna Artioli
abstract: Background Heart failure profoundly affects women's physical, emotional, and social well-being, often generating fear, uncertainty, and vulnerability that challenge adaptation and self-care. This study explored how women living with heart failure construct meaning and develop inner strength through illness awareness — defined as understanding the nature, severity, progression, and self-management implications of heart failure. Many women initially showed limited recognition of the seriousness and long-term trajectory of the condition, sometimes perceiving it as less threatening than other diagnoses (e.g., oncological conditions) and occasionally discontinuing treatment during periods of symptomatic improvement. The study also examined how awareness interacts with relationships and everyday adaptation. Methods A qualitative design was applied using reflexive thematic analysis based on in-depth, semi-structured interviews with eleven women recruited from a cardiology research hospital in Northern Italy. Data were analyzed through a six-phase analytical framework to identify patterns of meaning and transformation. Results Four interconnected themes described a developmental process of learning and adaptation: confronting vulnerability, reconnecting through others and faith, adapting daily life, and developing illness awareness and self-care. Participants revealed a gradual shift from emotional distress to reflective resilience, with awareness and self-reflection acting as catalysts for personal growth and empowerment. Limited illness awareness — particularly regarding disease severity, chronic progression, and the need for continuous treatment — conversely hindered adaptation and promoted passive coping. Conclusions Developing illness awareness emerged as both an educational and therapeutic that fosters resilience, self-reflection, and active engagement in self-care. Integrating structured educational and psychosocial interventions into heart failure management may strengthen women's inner resources and enhance their capacity to live meaningfully with chronic illness.

title: QSAR Modeling and Fragment Contribution Analysis of N-Benzyltryptamines at Human 5-HT2 Receptor Subtypes
authors: Vladimir V. Đorđević; Iva Binić; Jovana Petrović; Jelena Stojanov; Žarko J. Mitić; Aleksandar M. Veselinović
abstract: Serotonin 5-HT2 receptor agonists are returning to psychiatric drug development, but separating the three receptor subtypes pharmacologically remains difficult, and agonism at 5-HT2B carries a risk of valvular heart disease. A recent study reported affinities of 46 N-benzyltryptamines and N-benzyl-5-methoxytryptamines at all three human subtypes and analyzed them with an additive substituent model, which gave fragment coefficients of the same sign at every subtype and suggested that selectivity within this scaffold would be hard to achieve. We revisited that conclusion with non-additive models built under a protocol designed for small datasets: fifty stratified partitions with all filtering and hyperparameter tuning inside each training set, external statistics reported as distributions, response permutation on three partitions per endpoint, and partitions that withhold an entire scaffold or an entire substitution position. We repeated the analysis with two descriptor sets that share no variables and are built on different principles. Penalized linear models were predictive and transferable, whereas gradient boosting reproduced the training set exactly, and neither tree ensemble transferred to a held-out scaffold. Fragment contributions at 5-HT2A and 5-HT2C correlated at 0.25 compared with 0.77 for whole-molecule affinities, and both descriptor sets gave the same figure within 0.01. All models failed on para-substituted analogs, which distance-based applicability-domain criteria did not flag, whereas models trained without the ortho or the meta block stayed above a mean-predictor baseline. Aggregation over the whole molecule, rather than descriptor choice, conceals subtype divergence. One group drives the divergence: the N-benzyl substituent raises the predicted 5-HT2A affinity and lowers the predicted 5-HT2C affinity; excluding it raised the correlation to 0.93.

title: Independent predictive value of the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio for severe cardiopulmonary symptoms in high altitude polycythemia
authors: Lu Dai; Wentao Wu; Tengyun Chen; Wenjin Sun; Qi Zhang; Qingqing Su; Yue-Nan Ni; Xuan Zhang
abstract: Background High altitude polycythemia (HAPC) is traditionally viewed as a homogeneous condition driven by absolute hypoxemia, while clinical symptom severity fails to correlate with hemoglobin levels. This study aimed to identify distinct clinical phenotypes in HAPC and evaluate novel predictive biomarkers. Methods A total of 198 patients with HAPC were analyzed. Unsupervised K-means clustering was performed based on standardized absolute counts of five peripheral leukocyte subsets. A pre-specified multivariable Firth penalized logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were utilized to evaluate the predictive capacity of the monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR). Results Clustering identified four distinct immunophenotypes. Baseline demographics, absolute residential altitude, and hemoglobin levels were statistically comparable across all groups. Interestingly, Cluster 2 emerged as a highly symptomatic cardiopulmonary phenotype, with quiescent systemic inflammatory markers and the lowest MLR but the highest incidence of breathlessness and palpitations (32.3%). Multivariable analysis demonstrated that patients in the lowest MLR quartile exhibited a significantly elevated risk of belonging to the Cluster 2 phenotype (OR: 33.764, 95% CI: 9.615-180.993, P<0.001) compared to those in the highest quartile. Furthermore, MLR demonstrated favorable diagnostic discrimination for identifying this specific phenotype, with an optimism-corrected area under the curve of 0.810. Conclusion HAPC exhibits substantial pathophysiological heterogeneity independent of erythrocytosis severity. The MLR serves as a potential, independent, and accessible surrogate biomarker for the early identification of patients at risk for severe cardiopulmonary symptoms, facilitating precision triage in high-altitude medicine.

title: Physicians’ perspectives on the impact of echocardiographic feedback: a qualitative interview study
authors: Anahita Behzadi; Hamed Tasdighi; Mohammad Mehdi Kiani; Amirhossein Fatahpour
abstract: Echocardiography is a widely used non-invasive imaging modality central to diagnosing and monitoring heart failure, valvular disease, congenital heart disease, and cardiomyopathy. However, inappropriate requests, variability in reporting quality, and limited follow-up of diagnostic performance remain concerns, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Audit and feedback is an established strategy for improving professional practice, but its application in echocardiography remains underdeveloped. This study aimed to explore physicians’ perspectives on how the impact of echocardiographic feedback on clinicians can be assessed in Iran. A qualitative study was conducted using semi-structured interviews with an inductive approach and reflexive thematic analysis, following Braun and Clarke’s six-phase framework. From August 2022 to September 2023, 30 semi-structured interviews were conducted with purposively sampled participants, including cardiologists, university faculty in statistics, biostatistics, and health sciences, health insurance experts, and physicians working in health insurance organizations and research centers. The average interview duration was 49 min. Data saturation was reached after interview 27. Transcripts were coded by two independent researchers using MAXQDA 20 software. Trustworthiness was ensured using Lincoln and Guba’s criteria. The analysis generated five main themes and twelve subthemes: (1) indications for performing echocardiography; (2) diagnosing a patient’s need for echocardiography; (3) components of a complete echocardiography report; (4) sample selection and control group; and (5) data recording and analysis method. Participants emphasized the importance of guideline-based indications, standardized reporting, a before-and-after design with a control group, and the Difference-in-Differences (DID) technique for evaluating feedback. A cross-cutting finding regarding the role of body habitus and thoracic morphology in echocardiographic interpretation was integrated into the framework. The findings provide a comprehensive qualitative basis for a proposed framework for future quantitative evaluation of echocardiographic feedback. Future studies should operationalize these domains into valid and reliable indicators and prospectively evaluate whether feedback can improve the appropriateness, quality, and consistency of echocardiographic practice.

title: Elevated C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio is associated with early neurological deterioration in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective cohort study
authors: Zheng Zhou; Wenwen Xu; Zhaoping Wu; Tingting Duan; Ming Yang; Yueqi Xu; Junnan Ye
abstract: Background Early neurological deterioration (END) is a frequent complication of acute ischemic stroke (AIS) that contributes to poor clinical outcomes. The C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) reflects systemic inflammation relative to albumin levels and may be associated with END. We evaluated the association between log 2 -transformed CAR and END in patients with AIS. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 1,766 patients with AIS admitted between September 2016 to September 2022. END was defined as an increase of ≥2 points in the NIHSS motor item or total score within 72 h of admission. Associations between log₂-CAR and END were assessed using a multivariable logistic regression analysis. Generalized additive and two-piecewise regression models were used as exploratory analyses to assess potential non-linearity. ROC curves were used to compare CAR with established biomarkers and the A2DS2 score. Conclusion Higher CAR was independently associated with END in this cohort. CAR’s strongest predictive advantage was observed when compared with the A2DS2 clinical score, whereas superiority over CRP alone was not demonstrated. The possible threshold at a raw CAR of approximately 0.020 is exploratory and requires independent validation.

title: Associations between sex and traditional Chinese medicine body constitutions: the potential role of lifestyle behaviors in a cross-sectional study
authors: Cheng‐Hung Lee; Yichang Su; Chia‐Ing Li; Chuan‐Wei Yang; Tsai-Chung Li
abstract: Introduction This study investigated whether smoking, alcohol consumption, and physical inactivity mediate the associations between sex and Traditional Chinese Medicine body constitutions. Methods We analyzed data from 35,456 adults aged >18 years enrolled in the Taiwan Biobank. Body constitutions (yang deficiency, yin deficiency, and phlegm-stasis) were assessed using the Body Constitution Questionnaire (BCQ). The BCQ consists of 44 items. Each item is rated on a five-point Likert scale ranging from 1 (“never”) to 5 (“always”), with higher scores indicating a greater tendency toward the corresponding body constitution. Lifestyle behaviors included smoking, alcohol consumption, and leisure-time physical inactivity. Multivariable logistic regression and mediation analyses were performed. Results Female sex was independently associated with increased odds of yang deficiency [odds ratio (OR) = 2.52, 95% confidence interval (CI): 2.34–2.71], yin deficiency (OR = 2.09, 95% CI: 1.95–2.25), and phlegm-stasis (OR = 3.03, 95% CI: 2.79–3.30). Smoking showed significant negative indirect association, whereas alcohol consumption exhibited minimal mediation. Physical inactivity statistically accounted for approximately 6% of the observed associations between female sex and all three body constitution patterns. Discussion Women were more likely than men to exhibit yang deficiency, yin deficiency, and phlegm-stasis constitutions. Lifestyle behaviors explained only a small proportion of these sex differences. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should be interpreted as statistical associations rather than evidence of causal mediation.

title: Seasonal Initiation of Hemodialysis: A Single-Center Experience
authors: Derya Basak Tanburoglu; Emrah Günay; Hatice Gecol; İbrahim Dayanan; M Arslan; Gökçe Paşa
abstract: Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the seasonal pattern of hemodialysis initiation in a warm/subtropical climate region (Adana) and its association with the mode of initiation, early complications, and mortality. Materials and Methods: A total of 319 patients who started chronic hemodialysis at Adana City Training and Research Hospital, Department of Nephrology, between 2022 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Chi-square/Fisher’s exact and Kruskal–Wallis tests were used for seasonal comparisons. Multivariable logistic regression models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes, hypertension, and cardiovascular disease (coronary artery and/or valvular heart disease) were fitted for emergent initiation and for any early (30-day) complication, with a likelihood-ratio test of season as a whole; 3-month mortality (13 events) was described by season and analyzed with a season-only Firth model. Catheter dysfunction was analyzed among catheter-exposed patients, followed by sensitivity analyses. Results: A total of 58.3% of patients started dialysis emergently and 41.7% in a planned manner; only 11.3% had an arteriovenous fistula as initial vascular access. No significant seasonal differences were found in initiation type, indications, or the frequency of any early complication (161/314, 51.3%; p = 0.090). In the adjusted complication model, spring versus summer gave OR = 2.33 (95% CI: 1.23–4.41, p = 0.009; Holm-adjusted p = 0.028 across the three season contrasts), but the omnibus test of seasons was not significant (p = 0.069), and spring did not differ significantly from autumn or winter. Among catheter-exposed patients, catheter dysfunction occurred in 31.4% (22/70) in the spring and 16.5% (13/79) in the summer (p = 0.035; four-season omnibus p = 0.191); this contrast was not significant after excluding initiations from February to December 2023 (p = 0.111) or when the season was assigned at the midpoint of the risk window (p = 0.114). Season was not associated with emergent initiation (omnibus p = 0.230) or with 3-month mortality (Firth OR for spring versus summer 1.12, 95% CI: 0.28–4.48). Conclusions: Hemodialysis initiation in Adana was not associated with a winter-peak pattern in initiation counts or blood pressure. Spring initiation was associated with a higher frequency of early complications, mainly catheter dysfunction, but this exploratory single-center finding was not supported by the four-season omnibus tests and was sensitive to analytic choices, and none of the 33 seasonal omnibus tests remained significant after Holm correction. It is hypothesis-generating only and does not support a seasonal practice recommendation; confirmation in larger, multicenter, prospective studies is needed.

title: Antecedents and consequences of Green-tech FDI in emerging markets
authors: Zhuoran Liu
abstract: As environmental pressures intensify, attracting sustainable foreign direct investment (FDI), particularly green-tech FDI, has become a critical pathway for emerging markets to achieve environmental sustainability. However, existing research remains fragmented, offering limited insights into why green-tech FDI enters emerging markets and how it affects regional green innovation. This thesis addresses these gaps by systematically examining both the antecedents and consequences of green-tech FDI through three empirical studies using regional data from China. Study 1 and Study 2 focus on the antecedents of green-tech FDI. Study 1 examines how host-country conditions can attract green-tech FDI, highlighting the role of environmental management information disclosure (EMID) by domestic firms in reducing information gaps and strengthening green market–seeking motives. Study 2 shifts attention to the active decision-making of green-tech FDI, showing that under uncertainty, green-tech foreign investors engage in identity-based bandwagon learning by imitating peers with similar green identities, thereby mitigating investment risks. Study 3 turns to the consequences of green-tech FDI. It demonstrates that, due to the technological complexity of green innovation and limited absorptive capacity in emerging markets, green-tech FDI may generate crowding-out effects rather than purely positive spillovers. Adopting a network perspective, the study further finds that universities play a key moderating role: through broad linkages and deep collaborations, they help mitigate negative spillovers and facilitate the diffusion of green technologies. Together, the three studies advance the literature on sustainable FDI by differentiating green-tech FDI from general FDI and identifying the specific mechanisms that shape its entry decisions and local innovation outcomes. Practically, the findings provide guidance for emerging-market governments and firms on how to attract and manage sustainable investment, balance growth with environmental objectives, and strengthen local innovation ecosystems.

title: Combating Data and Target Shifts in Visual Tasks
authors: Zhaorui Tan
abstract: The rapid advancement of deep learning models for visual tasks has led to significant progress in many domains. However, a key challenge remains: ensuring that models can generalize effectively to unseen samples or novel classes, especially in real-world scenarios where training data-target pairs are often limited or unavailable, and test data may exhibit shifts in both data and targets. This thesis addresses the problem of shifts across data and targets, proposing novel methods to improve model generalization and transferability in complex settings. The thesis identifies the different shift scenarios for visual tasks and presents their problem forms. The research first relaxes the static target distribution assumption in Multi-Domain Generalization (mDG) tasks, introducing the General Multi-Domain Generalization (GMDG) objective to improve generalization under varying data shifts. Specifically, Extensive experiments validate that GMDG is feasible for classification, segmentation, and regression tasks. Further considering extreme target distribution shifts where even unknown novel classes emerge, the study also explores logical regularization techniques for tasks such as Generalized Category Discovery (GCD), mDG+GCD, and Class Incremental Learning (CIL), proposing a sample-based logical regularization term (L-Reg) to enhance data-, target-, and all-shift generalization. Additionally, a partial logic framework is introduced to address challenges in CIL, enabling models to retain room for unknown classes during training. This is further extended by the Partial-Logic Regularization (PL-Reg), which improves generalization across GCD, mDG+GCD, and transferability for CIL tasks. Furthermore, the thesis proposes a novel Semantic-aware Data Augmentation (SADA) framework for cross-modality generalization in text-to-image synthesis (T2Isyn), text-image retrieval (TIR), and image-text retrieval (ITR) tasks. This framework ensures semantic preservation across text and image modalities, improving both semantic consistency and image quality in cross-modality tasks. The methods proposed in this thesis offer significant advancements in visual generalization and transfer scenarios, providing theoretical insights and practical solutions for handling data shifts, target shifts, and multi-modalities in complex scenarios. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, demonstrating their superior performance across a range of tasks.

title: Depth of Processing, learner aptitude, and the acquisition of L2 English grammatical structures
authors: Shweta Nigam
abstract: Depth of Processing (DoP) is central to several models of instructed second language acquisition (ISLA) (Leow, 2015). While DoP has been extensively examined in vocabulary learning (e.g., Laufer & Hulstijn, 2001), its role in the acquisition of grammatical structures, particularly through oral and audio-visual modalities remains comparatively underexplored. Drawing on the Levels of Processing framework (Craik & Lockhart, 1972), this study investigated whether task-induced processing depth influences the acquisition of third conditionals and comparatives, and whether language aptitude (LLAMA B, D, F) predicts learning gains. Using a pretest–posttest design, four intact classes involving 108 Grade 8 EFL learners in India were assigned to one of the three experimental conditions differing in level and type of processing: Low DoP, High DoP Explicit, and High DoP Implicit. The treatment task required the participants to listen to an audio-visual story containing the target structures (third conditionals and comparatives) and complete analytic tasks (varying in different groups) before listening to the story for a second time. The oral performance of the participants was analysed for accuracy, and frequency of use of the target structures. A grammaticality judgement test (GJT) and an elicited imitation task (EIT) were used to assess the participants’ gains in the knowledge of the target structures. In addition, language aptitude (LLAMA B, D, F) was measured and modelled as a predictor of gain scores. Results showed a significant effect of processing condition on GJT performance with the High DoP Implicit group outperforming the High DoP Explicit group on total scores and comparatives. In contrast, ANCOVA analyses indicated no significant group differences on EIT outcomes once pretest performance was controlled, with pretest scores strongly predicting posttest performance. In oral production, processing effects were structure-specific: the Low DoP group showed greater accuracy gains for comparatives, while both High DoP groups revealed increased frequency of use of third conditionals. However, across all four measures, multiple regression analyses indicated that LLAMA B, D, and F did not significantly predict gain scores. Overall, the findings support a processing-by-structure pattern: deeper processing benefits were most evident for the more salient structure (comparatives) on an explicit, written measure, whereas complex, low-salience forms (third conditionals) showed limited accuracy change but increased frequency of use under deeper processing.

title: A UAV-Based Framework for Community-Scale Residential Building Energy Modelling in China
authors: Mengfan Jin
abstract: With increasing emphasis on energy efficiency and carbon emission reduction in the building sector, rapid and scalable energy modelling of existing buildings is critical for retrofit projects and policy development. Conventional surveys, data collection and energy modelling processes remain labour-intensive and impractical for large-scale applications, and energy modelling often dominates project time and cost. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) equipped with high-resolution and infrared cameras now offer fast and safe exterior surveys, showing great potential in building energy assessments. Yet, a systematic framework for UAV integration, from image capture through processing to inputs for building energy simulation, has not been established. This research addresses these challenges by developing a structured framework for community-scale building energy modelling, which integrates UAV photogrammetry to accelerate data acquisition, reduce labour, and shorten energy modelling time for retrofit projects. The framework is designed to minimise prior data requirements while maximising automation and retaining sufficient accuracy and reliability. It also addressed systemic issues, such as the lack of data necessary to fully exploit the potential of available technologies in the context of this study. To achieve this research objective, a mixed-methodology approach, combining desk studies and fieldwork, was adopted. First, a comprehensive review of UAV-based building energy studies mapped the current applications and available tools, proposing a preliminary framework. Fieldwork then encompassed a pilot study and a detailed case study. In the pilot test, a single building was surveyed to identify an optimal toolchain for flight planning, image capture, photogrammetric reconstruction, model generation, and selection of a simulation platform. The resulting refined framework was applied to a case study of a 39-building community, and it was demonstrated that further automation was necessary. The potential for automation was then further explored. Geomatic algorithms, machine learning, and deep learning techniques were compared, and the combination that best balanced accuracy and processing time was selected for 3D model generation and window-to-wall ratio (WWR) extraction. In parallel, an archetype library of residential buildings in the Hot Summer Cold Winter (HSCW) zone in China was compiled to facilitate the assignment of thermal parameters. Finally, a reusable community-scale building energy modelling (CBEM) workflow was assembled in Grasshopper using Ladybug Tools components to process the aforementioned inputs. In conclusion, this study integrates UAV photogrammetry, GIS-based geomatic algorithms, machine learning, and graphical programming to develop an UAV-CBEM framework. The outcomes establish a foundation for scalable UAV-based building energy assessments, enhancing applicability in data-limited and large-scale settings worldwide.

title: Spectral Materialism: Encounters with land-time-scapes
authors: Nightingale, Sam
abstract: This transdisciplinary, practice-based PhD introduces spectral materialism through art-based research encounters with ecologically and historically stratified land-time-scapes shaped by hypersalinity and colonial terraforming. Centred in the semi-arid Mallee (southeastern Australia) and read through echoes with California’s Imperial Valley, the project examines how spectral time—the co-presence and haunting of other temporalities—manifests in the material conditions of salt, soil, water, plants, and infrastructures. It asks how learning from geological, First Nations, colonial, and ecological pasts can orient responsibilities in unsettled futures. Treating the present as a crisis of time as much as a crisis of matter, the thesis critiques linear-progressive temporalities bound to Western modernity and extractive regimes. In response, spectral materialism is developed as both a conceptual framework and a critical creative methodology. Through alchemical media experiments with salt crystals, hypersaline soils, and halophytes, photography is reconfigured as a site-responsive, process-oriented practice. Salt is engaged as a material agent and ‘time-crystal’ whose phase shifts—dissolution, saturation, precipitation, crystallisation, evaporation—form a meta-chemistry that refracts deep-marine pasts, settler-colonial irrigation infrastructures, and contemporary dust into processual renderings of time. Methodologically, the project advances attunement as a mode of sensing and responsiveness to forces that are not always immediately perceptible yet are materially active. Field notes appear as para-writing, interrupting linear narration so that heterogeneous times co-present themselves within the text. The thesis is guided by First Nations temporalities—time as relational and in place—while remaining accountable to ethical limits and protocols. The contribution is twofold: a theoretical articulation of spectral materialism as a way to think time otherwise, and a set of site-responsive methods for engaging elemental media in saline environments. Together, they generate materially grounded accounts of spectral presences and open alternative pathways for knowing, sensing, and relating within land-time-scapes marked by enduring colonial and ecological afterlives amid planetary change.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO ACCELERATE DERMATOLOGICAL DISCOVERY
authors: Jasson Makkar
abstract: The skin is the largest and outermost organ that surrounds the human body and provides a physical barrier that protects the more delicate internal tissues from the harsh surrounding environment. Over the course of evolution, specialized structures have also arisen in the skin, including sweat and sebaceous glands, nails and claws, and hair follicles. The hair follicle is a multi-lineage mini-organ that is a critical component in defining mammalian species. The gain of function derived from hair and fur benefited these species for millennia due to its insulative and protective properties, mechanosensing function, and ability to serve as camouflage. Current approaches to assess these fibers are generally non-quantitative or are low throughput due to technical limitations of ‘splitting hairs’. We developed a novel deep learning-based computer vision approach for the high throughput quantification of individual hair fibers at a high resolution. Our innovative computer vision tool can distinguish and extract overlapping fibers for quantification of multivariate features including length, width, and color to generate single-hair phenomes (shPhenome) of diverse conditions across the lifespan of mice. Using our tool, we explored the effects of hormone signaling, genetic modifications, and aging on hair follicle output. These analyses revealed novel hair phenotypes as a result of endocrinological, developmental, and aging-related alterations in the fur coats of mice. This tool was then adapted to capture more nuanced hair phenotypes, such as curvature, in a variety of mouse models harboring genetic perturbations. Commercialization of the deep hair phenomics technology presented a unique opportunity to pursue research translation, transforming fundamental biological research into marketable products. Much like the traditional academic route, the path to commercialization requires consistent and continuous iteration, testing of hypotheses, and allowing data to influence and lead subsequent actions. However, as opposed to the pursuit of knowledge, translating research into market-ready solutions requires a focus on consumer needs and the identification of market opportunities. Additionally, the shift in incentive structure requires commercial ventures to prioritize intellectual property protection, alter capital and resource allocation, and seek alternative fundraising sources. The entrepreneurial foundation built through this process culminated in the filing of a provisional patent and establishment of a startup company, kerat Inc. This journey illuminated the multifaceted challenges inherent in closing the gap between academic innovation and commercially viable goods, requiring simultaneous advancement of technical capabilities, adaptation to market dynamics, and fabrication of business infrastructure. Overall, the culmination of work presented in this dissertation sheds light on the importance of quantitatively assessing hair fiber properties to capture the biological phenomena that underlie this fundamental feature of mammalian skin. These findings also highlight the capabilities of this methodology for identifying perturbations in normal growth, potentially indicative of disease or dysfunction. Lastly, this showcased the potential of this technology’s commercial use cases in both the cosmetics and diagnostics industries.

title: Contested urbanisms: The politics of heritage and housing in Jakarta’s kampungs
authors: Binte Masron, Irna Nurlina
abstract: Do heritage-making projects resist or advance gentrification in Southeast Asia? Like other Global South cities, contested urbanisms chequer Jakarta’s postcolonial urban landscape. Competing ideas about urban development manifest in various ways of seeing and producing the city, as demonstrated by evictions, revitalisation projects, and informal housing. Increased evictions of urban villages (urban kampungs) between 2013 and 2018 in Jakarta saw growing grassroots heritage movements as part of a spectrum of resistance to top-down urban management by state and private sector actors who also stake their claims on what ‘heritage’ is. These tensions amongst the political projects of various actors led me to ask: how do heritage-making projects of/by urban villages affect housing conditions in Jakarta, with reference to gentrification-led displacement? Using ethnographic methods and thematic analysis, I delve into the constructions of heritage, the impact of heritage-making on housing security for residents, and the broader political impact of heritage-making from above and below in Jakarta’s Kota Tua and two of its kampungs, Luar Batang and Pekojan. I argue that the dominant heritage constructions in Kota Tua demonstrate a top-down logic that emphasises infrastructure and the built environment with strong private sector presence, which impact the kampungs in varied ways. Findings showed that top-down heritage-making demonstrates higher likelihood of driving gentrification through the commodification of space, prioritising capital and material values. Residents and their advocates employ heritage-making from below in various forms to reclaim their place in the city as they face various forms of displacement, with unanticipated consequences. The processes of heritage-making from above and below reveal the connections and disjunctures between different authorities which subaltern actors work through, producing new politics that contest or entrench existing conditions. The findings contribute to the theorising of the politics of gentrification in heritage and urban studies, and a deeper understanding of Jakarta’s Old Town.

title: From Sparse to Dense: Label-Efficient Weakly Supervised Segmentation for Images and Videos
authors: Wang, Jian
abstract: Obtaining high-quality annotated data has become a primary bottleneck for training deep learning models, particularly for dense prediction tasks like semantic segmentation and video salient object segmentation. The demand for meticulous, pixel-level labeling makes fully-supervised approaches prohibitively expensive and limits their scalability. This thesis directly confronts this issue by proposing and systematically investigating a label-efficient "sparse-to-dense'' paradigm. The core objective is to develop innovative frameworks that can learn from sparse, inexpensive weak supervision—such as image-level tags or scribbles—and intelligently propagate this minimal information to generate complete, pixel-accurate dense predictions. The major part of this thesis focuses on the "sparse-to-dense'' challenge within Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) for images, where models learn from only image-level tags. Dominant approaches rely on Class Activation Maps (CAMs) as initial object seeds. However, CAMs inherently activate only the most discriminative object regions, leading to incomplete pseudo-labels. This gives rise to the central problem of activation densification: the critical process of expanding these sparse activations to cover the full extent of an object. Our research addresses this challenge through a progressive, multi-faceted strategy. Our exploration begins with a foundational framework (C3) designed to rectify the intrinsic flaws of initial CAMs. We propose a synergistic mutual calibration method. This method leverages the discrepancies between the two maps to generate local prototypes, which are simultaneously utilized to complete missing object parts and suppress background noise, yielding a significantly more accurate and complete initial seed. This foundational work immediately reveals the limitation of single-prototype instability and its inability to capture diverse features. Building on this foundation, we then develop architecture-specific strategies to address deeper limitations of the prototype-based approach. For Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) (C4), the use of a single prototype proves insufficient to capture significant intra-class variation. In response, we introduce an Optimal Transport (OT)-assisted framework that effectively mines multiple, diverse prototypes, thereby yielding more comprehensive activation maps. However, while C4 solves the intra-class diversity problem, the inherent local context constraint of the CNN architecture becomes the new bottleneck, fundamentally limiting the quality of globally-aware feature extraction needed for optimal multi-prototype assignment. This limitation necessitates a shift in architectural focus from CNNs to Vision Transformers. In the ViT architecture (C5), a new challenge arises where the token gap between the discriminative class token and varied patch tokens leads to incomplete activation. To bridge this gap, we leverage a tailored application of Optimal Transport, where the algorithm is tasked with learning a comprehensive proxy to ensure complete object activation. Despite these architectural advances (C3-C5), the overall WSSS performance hit a ceiling. This is fundamentally limited by the sparse supervision of class labels, which cannot provide precise boundary information. To break this ceiling, our WSSS exploration culminates in a universal enhancement strategy (C6) that transcends architecture-specific designs by leveraging Visual Foundation Models (VFMs). We resolve the conflict between the discriminative nature of initial CAMs and the VFM's need for holistic prompts. By modeling the CAM foreground as a graph and employing spectral analysis, our method intelligently selects a diverse set of prompt points that represent the overall structure of the foreground object. This guides the VFM to generate superior, boundary-aware supervision that can universally enhance any WSSS pipeline. Subsequently, the thesis extends the "sparse-to-dense'' paradigm to the dynamic domain of video, addressing Weakly Supervised Video Salient Object Segmentation (WSVSOS) (C7) from sparse scribble annotations. In this specific context, the challenge evolves into spatio-temporal densification, which requires both full-object coverage within each frame and temporal consistency across the video sequences. To this end, we introduce the core CFMR framework, which utilizes Spatio-Temporal co-regulation. This framework is subsequently enhanced (CFMR+) by integrating the VFM guidance strategy from C6, which provides high-quality spatial priors essential for ensuring both high spatial detail and inter-frame consistency. By enforcing both intra-frame and cross-frame consistency between these two streams, our method effectively propagates the sparse initial signal to generate dense and temporally coherent saliency masks. In conclusion, this thesis presents a comprehensive and cohesive investigation into label-efficient segmentation tasks, offering a suite of innovative and effective strategies for the "sparse-to-dense'' challenge. Our work establishes a progressive roadmap that systematically overcomes architectural and semantic limitations, culminating in highly robust and generalized densification pipelines. Our extensive experimental results on standard benchmarks validate the state-of-the-art performance of these methods, providing robust solutions to a long-standing problem in the computer vision field.

title: Unsupervised Deep-learning Methods for Low-dose Computed Tomography Reconstruction
authors: An, Ran
abstract: Computed tomography (CT) has become an indispensable imaging technique in medical diagnostics and industrial applications, owing to its non-invasive nature and high resolution in visualizing object internal structures. While X-ray CT (X-ray computed tomography) significantly enhances lesion detection capabilities, excessive exposure to X-ray radiation raises substantial health concerns, including elevated cancer risks and potential genetic damage. Although low-dose CT (LDCT) protocols reduce radiation safety concerns, they inevitably introduce severe noise and artifacts, which might compromise diagnostic accuracy. Recent advances in supervised deep learning approaches have demonstrated remarkable success in LDCT reconstruction. However, the reliance on paired training data severely limits their deployment in practical CT applications. This fundamental constraint highlights the critical importance of developing unsupervised reconstruction methods. Although existing unsupervised LDCT methods have made notable progress, they still face challenges requiring systematic solutions. This thesis makes three contributions to advance the field of unsupervised LDCT reconstruction: 1. Current dual-domain self-supervised LDCT denoising methods typically neglect the heterogeneity of the non-stationary Gaussian noise levels in low-dose sinograms and usually treat them as common images without appropriately controlling the denoising strength. The denoisers employed by them, which are based on classic convolutional neural networks (CNN), will lead to blurring artifacts in the reconstructed images if directly used for sinogram denoising. In addition, the denoising strength in the sinogram and image domains must be well-balanced to avoid introducing over-blurring or secondary artifacts in the reconstructed images, but existing approaches do not focus on this crucial point. To address these limitations, this thesis proposes a novel end-to-end dual-domain self-supervised framework for LDCT denoising. It employs Dropblock layers to adaptively localize the effect of convolution for sinogram denoising and sets a weighted average between the denoised sinograms and their noisy counterparts to better control the denoising strength, thus effectively reducing the blurring artifacts and leading to a well-balanced dual-domain denoising. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed method. 2. Existing normalizing flows (NFs)-based unsupervised LDCT reconstruction methods face challenges in both image quality and computational efficiency. On one hand, they typically utilize a two-way transformation strategy between noisy images and latent variables, which could easily lead to detail loss and secondary artifacts in the reconstructed images. On the other hand, training NFs on high-resolution CT images is computationally intensive. Although conditional normalizing flows (CNFs) can mitigate computational costs by learning conditional probabilities, existing approaches rely on labeled data for conditionalization, leaving unsupervised CNFs-based LDCT reconstruction a challenge. To tackle these issues, this thesis proposes a novel unsupervised LDCT iterative reconstruction algorithm based on CNFs. The proposed method employs a strict one-way transformation strategy during the alternating optimization in the dual spaces to prevent detail loss and secondary artifacts, and proposes a novel unsupervised conditionalization strategy for CNFs, thus achieving efficient training and inference on high-resolution images. The proposed method illustrates high-quality and relatively fast unsupervised reconstruction. Experiments across two datasets demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method by rivaling several state-of-the-art methods. 3. Current diffusion model-based LDCT reconstruction methods solely employ the prior distributions learned from normal-dose CT data but neglect the valuable priors in low-dose data, which contain information about the characteristics of low-dose noise and artifacts. In addition, their reconstruction speed suffers from multiple sampling steps, presenting low efficiency. Breaking new ground in prior utilization, this thesis proposes a novel unsupervised LDCT iterative reconstruction algorithm based on dual denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM), which leverages both normal-dose and low-dose priors. Specifically, the proposed method employs two DDPMs to learn the prior distributions from normal-dose and low-dose images, respectively, and incorporates them into a joint iterative reconstruction framework. To accelerate the reconstruction, partial diffusion sampling and single-pass deterministic reconstruction strategy are utilized in the proposed method, as well as the spaced OS-SART approaches. Experiments at different dose levels demonstrate the outstanding performance and fast speed of the proposed reconstruction algorithm. Through these innovations and contributions, this thesis addresses some significant challenges in current deep-learning-based unsupervised LDCT reconstruction methods, and proposes three novel unsupervised reconstruction algorithms. The proposed methods effectively improve the performance and efficiency of LDCT reconstruction under different unsupervised learning conditions, and provide some new perspectives and inspirations for future research.

authors: Ji Yun; Ville Tiusanen; Konsta Karttunen; Divyesh Patel; Esa Pitkänen; Biswajyoti Sahu
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Overview This record accompanies the manuscript "Deep learning reveals distinct and complementary cis-regulatory grammar from STARR-seq and lentiMPRA". The archive contains processed data, analysis workflows, selected model artifacts, source records, and figure-level outputs used to compare episomal genomic STARR-seq and integrated lentivirus-based MPRA in HepG2 cells. The study integrates assay signal comparison, cCRE and epigenomic annotation, transcription factor ChIP-seq correlation, motif enrichment, regression-based motif activity analysis, and sequence-based deep learning to characterize shared and assay-specific cis-regulatory grammar. Contents This release includes: processed STARR-seq and lentiMPRA analysis inputs; DeepSTARR FASTA/TSV model input files; lentiMPRA probe-level and STARR-seq peak-level activity tables; selected raw/source files redistributed with the release; public accession tables and source-resource inventories; JASPAR 2024 motif files and transcription factor annotation tables; workflow scripts for data preparation, signal comparison, motif analysis, model training and evaluation, and supplementary analyses; MEIRLOP and GimmeMotifs result tables and figure outputs; trained DeepSTARR baseline model files, held-out test splits, predictions, and performance summaries; manuscript figures and supplementary outputs; environment/version notes; MANIFEST.tsv and checksums.tsv for file inventory and SHA256 verification. Workflow Modules The release is organized into the following workflow modules: 01_data_preparation 02_signal_comparison 03_chip_epigenome_correlation 04_meirlop 05_gimmemotifs 06_deepstarr 07_supplementary_features MPRALegnet.tar.gz Each module contains the scripts, intermediate outputs, and documentation required to reproduce the corresponding analyses. Scope and External Inputs This archive provides a reproducible snapshot of the computational analyses performed for the manuscript. Original public datasets are not redistributed and should be downloaded from their respective repositories using the accession tables and references provided in the manuscript and accompanying source files. Large third-party resources, including the GRCh38 reference genome and selected ENCODE ChIP-seq and epigenomic bigWig files, are documented but not bundled. Their expected locations and regeneration instructions are described in the workflow README files. This release includes DeepSTARR model artifacts. MPRALegNet training, attribution analyses, TF-MoDISco results, and associated model files are documented as deferred components and are not included in this release.
